articles.title: LeBron James’ Wife Under Fire After Saying She’s Not ‘Responsible’ For Friends’ First-Class Flight
articles.summary: LeBron James‘ wife, Savannah, is under fire after her friend revealed that she doesn’t fly first class with her. On […]
articles.body:
Savannah James faces backlash after friend reveals they fly in different classes, sparking debate on social media.

Savannah James and her friend discuss their different lifestyles and how they navigate their friendship when it comes to travel.

Some users defend Savannah James, pointing out that her husband LeBron James is the one funding their flights and emphasizing the importance of financial independence.

LeBron James ' wife, Savannah , is under fire after her friend revealed that she doesn't fly first class with her. On an episode of Boardroom's "Mental Wealth" podcast, Savannah and her longtime friend and podcast co-host, April McDaniel, discussed money and how it affects their friendship. The pair's answers went viral online, sparking passionate responses from fans who believe Savannah isn't doing enough.

LeBron James' Wife, Savannah, Says Her Friends Don't Have An Expectation Of Her

"My friends are very respectful of my situation. You know, if I'm like, 'We're going somewhere,' they already understand what it is," Savannah said on the Monday, September 28 episode of "Mental Wealth."

She continued, "There's no expectation of, like, taking care of something or, you know, just having me be responsible for them. It has never, ever been that."

As the conversation continued, Savannah's friend, McDaniel, revealed that their lifestyles are different. She said the differences show up when they travel, explaining that she flies business class while Savannah flies first class.

"We talk about this a lot because there's two different lifestyles that exist," said McDaniel. "Like we're not delusional to that. And I think Savannah has accommodated where I'm at."

Savannah James Gives Her Friends Notice Before A Lavish Trip

McDaniel and Savannah have been spotted together on lavish trips and outings before. The pair even spoke about shopping together at luxury stores while abroad. However, McDaniel said that those trips take advance planning.

"We're planning out. Like, we don't just show up at Fashion Week week-of. We don't move like that even though people think we do," she said.

While money has never been a point of contention between the pair, McDaniel said some outsiders have been overly critical of their relationship.

"People were very critical of her being in first [class] and me being in business and me going up to first and getting in her bed and watching a movie. It was, like, offended," she said.

LeBron James adds a new business venture to his portfolio.

The NBA champion is also starting a new YouTube channel .

Magic Johnson reacted to news that the Los Angeles Lakers were sold to new owners .

LeBron James will play his first game against the defending NBA champions .

Savannah James Gets Backlash After Friend Reveals Rules Of Their Friendship

Savannah and McDaniel's statements went viral and prompted passionate responses from users who felt Savannah wasn't doing enough while being married to a certified billionaire.

"If I ever become a billionaire, my friends gone ball with me. Anybody agreeing with Savannah James is not a good friend, period. I'm done going back and forth with you," one person shared.

A second user agreed, adding, "There is absolutely NO way my best friend is flying different from me. The absolute least she could do was pay for the upgrade from business to first class."

Someone else said they weren't surprised by Savannah's comment before saying she seemed to have a "selfish spirit" in her.

"If I'm flying first class, so is my bff if it's in my power. Sometimes [people] love to remind you that you're beneath them in some way. I just couldn't be around that knowing that my friends are my sisters and I'm standing 10 toes down with them," they added.

LeBron Jame Gets Brought Into The Discussion

The comments weren't all bad, though. Some users defended Savannah and even brought LeBron into the equation.

"I want y'all to keep in mind that it's her HUSBAND's money… idk if y'all forgetting but technically, LeBron is funding the flights. Now, a lot of us may make sure we both fly first class, but to sit up here and tell her how to spend her HUSBAND'S money is nuts.

Another said, "Let's not forget that LeBron's money ain't Savannah's. People develop entitlement thinking that loving someone means financing them, and it doesn't. If she can and wants to, cool. If not, OK."

LeBron James Has Spoken About Money Before

According to The Blast , LeBron also takes protecting his money very seriously.

On a podcast, LeBron said he doesn't play when it comes to business. He added that when he met his financial advisor, the advisor gave him a stern warning.

"My financial advisor, the first thing I told him when he wanted to manage my money was, 'If you steal my money, bro, or if I'm broke, bro, I'm letting you know, bro, it ain't going to be good for you,'" he said.

Tem também uma série gravada em Brasília para mostrar o que acontece depois que deputados e senadores são eleitos. Como funcionam a Câmara, o Senado e as principais engrenagens do Congresso.

articles.title: Komal Rani Swarnkar REACTS amid affair rumours with Govinda; says, 'We will continue to be seen together, if that bothers anyone, let them burn'
articles.summary: Komal Rani Swarnkar, who is at the centre of the controversy over her alleged affair with actor Govinda, has responded to the criticism.
articles.body: Komal Rani Swarnkar, who is at the centre of the controversy over her alleged affair with actor Govinda, has responded to the criticism. On Friday, she posted a long note on her Instagram Stories, questioning why people are commenting so openly on her personal life.Komal Rani Swarnkar REACTS to her rumours of her affair with GovindaKomal Rani Swarnkar began by pointing to celebrities who have spoken about her and Govinda. She wrote, "Recently, I have seen some celebrities openly commenting on Govinda Ji and my personal life and our character. Yet I have never seen them come forward so strongly to express their opinion on any serious issue, whether it was terrorism, politics, the death of actors or even another actor's multiple marriages. Why, then, has our personal life suddenly become such a public spectacle that everyone feels entitled to comment on it?"Komal Rani Swarnkar defends her appearances with GovindaKomal Rani defended her public appearances with the actor, saying they were linked to their upcoming film. She asked, “Since when did going before Ganpati Bappa alongside my Hero and praying for the success of my upcoming Film, ‘Roopa’, become a matter of shame, a national issue or ‘Dikhawa’ for others?"She added, “We announced our film ‘Roopa’, not a romantic affair."She also asked her critics who they are to decide that the two appear together to show a personal relationship and not to promote the film. She said, “We are working together, and we will continue to be seen together. If that bothers anyone, let them burn."Komal Rani Swarnkar's sharp words for her criticsKomal also targeted some actresses in the industry without naming them. She wrote, “Some actresses in the film industry, whose careers have gone cold, whose films are no longer working at the box office, seem to have nothing left except their washed-out brand tags. They are trying to stay relevant by sticking their noses into other people's ongoing controversies and trying desperately to keep themselves in the limelight."She made it clear that she does not care what they think of her. “I honestly don't give a damn whether these people think I am good person or a bad one," she wrote. She added, “I feel they are all part of the same group, taking out their frustration over their own failed marriages on someone else."Komal Rani Swarnkar's reply to criticismFilm industry members such as Kashmera Shah and Divya Khossla had earlier criticised the actress for appearing with Govinda and made allegations against her.Without naming anyone, Komal asked people to stop linking themselves to her name. "Stop trying to stay relevant by constantly associating yourselves with my name. Perhaps the saying is true, ‘Your dignity is in your own hands’."She ended her note with a warning, writing, "People like that should know their limits and stop provoking others to the point where your own past may be exposed."Komal Rani Swarnkar and Govinda's film 'Roopa' is set to hit theatres in early 2027. articles.title: Quién es Esmeralda Moya, invitada hoy en 'Pasapalabra' que saltó a la fama en una serie que marcó a toda una generación en España
articles.standfirst: La actriz y modelo participa esta semana en el concurso de Antena 3
articles.summary: La actriz y modelo participa esta semana en el concurso de Antena 3
articles.body: El programa presentado por Roberto Leal es el rey del prime time en España. El concurso 'Pasapalabra' congrega cada día a más de dos millones de espectadores, quienes se aferran a la pequeña pantalla para ver cómo se ponen a prueba las diferentes personalidades del país. Además, los invitados semanales también es un atractivo para la audiencia. Esta semana, una de ellas es Esmeralda Moya. Esmeralda Moya Cañas nació el 31 de agosto de 1985 en Madrid y es una actriz y modelo. Con tan solo 16 años ya hacía campañas de publicidad para revistas tanto dentro como fuera de España. Su salto a televisión fue en 2006 con 'Círculo Rojo'. Tres años después apareció en '90-60-90' de Antena 3, pero su éxito lo conseguiría al año siguiente, en 2010, al interpretar a Claudia Ruano en 'Los Protegidos'. A raíz de ese reconocimiento en el panorama actoral español, Esmeralda Moya trabajó en '45 revoluciones'; 'Historias de protegidos' y 'Servir y proteger'. Los otros invitados de esta semana son Eduardo Navarrete, Elisabeth Reyes y Miquel Fernández. Los cuatro intentarán ayudar tanto a los concursantes para sumar segundos en el rosco y que, al fin, logren llevarse el bote.

articles.title: 'Outrageous': Halle Berry responds to ex-husband Olivier Martinez's restraining order, abuse allegations
articles.summary: Halle Berry speaks out against ex-husband Oliver Martinez amid his recent restraining order against the Oscar-winning star. He accuses Berry of physical abus...
articles.body:
Halle Berry is speaking out against her ex-husband Olivier Martinez, after he accused the actor of physically abusing their 12-year-old son and was granted a restraining order against the Oscar winner.

Marina Beck, an attorney for the 60-year-old "Catwoman" and "John Wick: Chapter 3" star, in a statement downplayed Martinez's protective order, granted Thursday by a Los Angeles Superior Court judge.

"To say this filing is entirely meritless and deliberately misleading would be an understatement," Beck said, later accusing Martinez of repeatedly violating court orders and interfering with "necessary therapeutic and educational interventions to the detriment" of his son with Berry.

The attorney added: "In a way, today's filing is not entirely unexpected from an individual with a well-documented history of erratic, possessive and violent behavior. Fortunately, Halle is used to this kind of outrageous conduct from Mr. Martinez and, while she is deeply saddened, she will not allow it to deter her from fighting for Maceo's best interests and providing him with the love and support he needs."

Patrick Baghdaserians, an attorney for Martinez, did not comment on the statement from Berry's legal team, but said the welfare and safety of Berry and Martinez's child remains paramount.

According to the order reviewed by The Times, Berry is prohibited from contacting Martinez, 60, and their son Maceo beyond the terms of her August 2023 split-custody agreement . The judge also modified the actor's visitation time, limiting her hours with her son to Mondays, Tuesdays and weekends between 10 a.m. and 8 p.m.

Berry and Martinez wed in France in July 2013, shortly after confirming they were expecting a baby together. They welcomed their son in October. Berry shares a daughter with ex-boyfriend Gabriel Aubry. The actor was also previously married to ex-MLB pro David Justice and singer-actor Eric Benét and is currently engaged to musician Van Hunt.

Berry filed to divorce Martinez in October 2015. Their divorce finally came to an end after eight years in August 2023, when they agreed to joint custody of their son and Berry agreed to pay Martinez $8,000 a month in child support. The "Monster's Ball" actor was also ordered at the time to also pay Martinez 4.3% of any income she receives above $2 million.

Martinez's request for a domestic violence restraining order centered on an alleged Sept. 26 incident involving Berry and their son. Martinez alleged the actor "physically abused our son, Maceo, by jumping on him, putting her hands around his neck, and choking him."

The financial terms of their divorce also appeared to be central to another alleged incident in 2023, when Berry allegedly told Maceo, then 9, that his father is " 'a white b— trying to rob a Black woman' due to child support issues," the request said. Martinez's filing included a declaration of Berry's alleged history of abuse, screenshots of his text conversation with Berry following the alleged September incident in which she appears to have written, "I feel terrible about what happened last night."

Martinez requested sole legal and physical custody of Maceo. He also asked that Berry refrain from drinking or partaking in other substances during her visitation time and asked that she complete sobriety testing "before, during and after" her visitation, according to court documents. The judge denied those sobriety testing requests until a further hearing for the order on Oct. 16.

Berry has been a vocal supporter for victims of domestic violence and a volunteer at the Jenesse Center, a nonprofit organization dedicated to domestic violence intervention and prevention. The actor has also spoken about her own experience with domestic violence growing up. She recalled her father's abusive treatment of her mother during a gala in 2015.

"She stayed for too long and her children, my sister and I, saw far too much and I've suffered the damage of being a child of domestic violence," Berry said at the time.

Former Times staff writer Jonah Valdez contributed to this report.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Bicame de Nova Lima é isolado após chuva alterar estrutura | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa Civil e equipes da AngloGold avaliam alterações identificadas na estrutura histórica de Nova Lima. Moradores próximos foram orientados a deixar o local.
articles.summary: Munumento histórico teve área isolada pela Defesa Civil e AngloGold, com evacuação preventiva de moradores vizinhos.
articles.body:
A área no entorno do Aqueduto Bicame, em Nova Lima, na região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte , foi isolada após a forte chuva registrada na tarde desta sexta-feira (2). Segundo a prefeitura, a medida foi adotada imediatamente depois que foi identificada uma alteração na estrutura.

A Defesa Civil isolou a área para que sejam feitas vistorias junto com a AngloGold Ashanti, responsável pela estrutura. Por segurança, moradores de residências próximas foram orientados a deixar o local.

Importante referência da paisagem urbana de Nova Lima, o Bicame foi escolhido por votação popular como símbolo da cidade. O patrimônio, construído em 1890, é tombado pelo município, conforme o Decreto Municipal nº 2.072, de 2 de abril de 2004.

O aqueduto foi construído abastecer de água a área industrial da mineração Morro Velho. A estrutura atravessa quatro ruas, formando arcos de passagem para veículos e pedestres.

Em 2024, uma restauração com investimento de aproximadamente R$ 3,6 milhões, foi feita no monumento histpor meio da Lei Federal de Incentivo à Cultura foi feita na estrutura.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Nova Lima, o projeto de restauração buscou causar o menor impacto possível para realinhar a estrutura e preservar as características originais do Bicame. A obra foi executada em parceria com a Engecop e a Construpower, com aprovação da APPA - Cultura & Patrimônio.

Em nota, a AngloGold informou que equipes de Engenharia e Suporte Operacional também estão no local avaliando as condições do Bicame e tomando as medidas necessárias. A empresa afirmou que a prioridade é garantir a segurança e avaliar tecnicamente os impactos das chuvas sobre a estrutura.

articles.title: Com 'João Bosco All Star Quintet', o cantor festeja 80 anos em show que teve Tiago Iorc e Hamilton de Holanda | G1
articles.standfirst: O roteiro do show estende comemoração ao parceiro fundamental do compositor, Aldir Blanc, que também estaria celebrando oito décadas de vida em 2026.
articles.summary: O roteiro do show estende comemoração ao parceiro fundamental do compositor, Aldir Blanc, que também estaria celebrando oito décadas de vida em 2026.
articles.body:
João Bosco (à direita) canta a música 'Perfeição' com o convidado Tiago Iorc na estreia carioca do show em que o artista mineiro festeja 80 anos de vida — Foto: Mauro Ferreira / g1

Data e local: 2 de outubro de 2026 no Qualistage (Rio de Janeiro, RJ)

♬ Ficou evidente ao longo das mais de duas horas do show “80 anos” que João Bosco celebrava no palco da casa carioca Qualistage não somente o próprio aniversário, mas também os 80 anos que Aldir Blanc (2 de setembro de 1946 – 4 de maio de 2020) – parceiro fundamental do compositor mineiro nos anos 1970 e 1980 – também estaria festejando em 2026.

A duplicidade da comemoração do show – derivado do recém-lançado álbum revisionista “Amigos novos e antigos” (2026) e estreado no Rio de Janeiro (RJ) na noite de ontem, sexta-feira, 2 de outubro – foi explicitada tanto nas imagens expostas no telão, com Aldir sendo recorrente nas projeções, como no roteiro, dominado por sambas apresentados pela dupla de compositores entre 1974 e 1982, em gravações feitas pelo próprio Bosco e/ou por cantoras como Elis Regina (1945 – 1982), Clementina de Jesus (1901 – 1987) e Simone.

O som não estava à altura de um gênio como João Bosco, mas jamais prejudicou a fluência de apresentação que teve com convidados o cantor Tiago Iorc – intérprete de “Perfeição” (João Bosco e Francisco Bosco, 2009), canção de aura bossa-novista gravada por Iorc com Bosco no álbum “Amigos novos e antigos” – e o bandolinista Hamilton de Holanda.

Virtuose do bandolim, Hamilton se afinou de imediato com a atmosfera jazzística de alguns arranjos e com a banda de sonhos. O “João Bosco All Star Quintet”, assim graciosamente rotulado pelo cantor em cena, era formado por Armando Marçal (percussão), Guto Wirtti (baixo), Kiko Freitas (bateria) e Ricardo Silveira (guitarra), além do próprio Bosco no inconfundível violão.

O quinteto virou sexteto com Hamilton de Holanda solando melodias e/ou acrescentando nuances nos sambas “Nação” (João Bosco, Aldir Blanc e Paulo Emílio, 1982), “Incompatibilidade de gênios” – número em que cada músico improvisou, em sintonia com o espírito jazzístico daquele momento – e no medley em que o cantor encadeou “Quilombo” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 1973), “Tiro de misericórdia” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 1977) e “Escadas da Penha” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 1975), fazendo a crônica social da violência urbana.

Uma das marcas registradas dos arranjos criados pelo trombonista Rafael Rocha para o álbum “Amigos novos e antigos” , os sopros estiveram ausentes no show, por incompatibilidade de agendas dos músicos arregimentados para o disco, o que criou outra pulsação para algumas músicas no confronto com as gravações do álbum – caso sobretudo do samba “Siri recheado e o cacete” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 1980).

Contudo, Bosco sempre soube se virar muito bem. E brilhou em cena, com a tarimba de ser cantor a quem basta somente um violão para fazer a magia acontecer. Por isso, o show resultou agradável. Com o “João Bosco All Star Quintet”, o artista caiu muito bem no suingue do samba “Boca de sapo” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 1979), evocando a aura de Clementina, com quem gravou a composição.

Ainda que sem a arquitetura mais sofisticada do show “Boca cheia de frutas” (2025), o roteiro do show “80 anos” cumpriu bem a intenção de compilar o suprassumo do cancioneiro autoral do compositor, um dos gigantes da MPB.

Aberto com o samba “Plataforma” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 1977), ao qual se seguiram os também infalíveis “Mestre-sala dos mares” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 1974) e “De frente pro crime” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 1974), este com citação da melodia de “Agora eu sou diretoria” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 2021), o roteiro do show “80 anos” surtiu maior efeito para a plateia – em geral, fria – na segunda metade da apresentação.

Foi quando Bosco disparou petardos como a canção das Árabias “Jade” (João Bosco, 1989), o refinado bolero “Quando o amor acontece” (João Bosco e Abel Silva, 1987), o samba “O bêbado e a equilibrista” (João Bosco e Aldir Blanc, 1979) – número que gerou manifestações políticas na plateia – e, claro, a balada “Papel machê” (João Bosco e José Carlos Capinan, 1984). Nessas duas últimas músicas, o coro da plateia se fez ouvir mais forte do que o canto de Bosco em momento de comunhão entre artista e público.

Contudo, João Bosco nunca faz show ao estilo de karaokê. O som do artista é também para ser contemplado porque, no palco, a música do artista está sempre em movimento, ainda que por vezes sutil.

Mesmo que o roteiro faça as necessárias concessões de um apresentação de caráter festivo que pede hits, “80 anos” é o show de um artista que nunca foi pelo caminho mais fácil para agradar e que, por isso mesmo, chega íntegro às oito décadas de vida, ainda e sempre em movimento.

articles.title: Festa da Padroeira Aparecida: novena começa com novo arcebispo | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação no Santuário Nacional terá duas celebrações diárias, além de procissão, carreata, passeio ciclístico e Festival da Padroeira.
articles.summary: A Festa da Padroeira Aparecida inicia a novena com celebrações diárias no Santuário Nacional, procissões e a estreia do arcebispo Dom Mário Antônio.
articles.body:
Começa neste sábado (3), em Aparecida (SP), a Novena e Festa da Padroeira do Brasil. A programação segue até 12 de outubro, Dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, e deve reunir milhares de fiéis no Santuário Nacional.

A edição deste ano marca a primeira Novena da Padroeira de Dom Mário Antônio da Silva como arcebispo de Aparecida , nomeado pelo Papa Leão XIV em março deste ano. Dom Mário substituiu Dom Orlando Brandes, que deixou o posto após uma década liderando a comunidade católica em Aparecida.

Neste ano, a novena tem como tema “Com Maria, em comunidade, conhecer e praticar a Palavra de Deus”. Durante os nove dias de preparação para a festa, os devotos são convidados a rezar, refletir e conhecer a Palavra de Deus, tendo Maria como exemplo de fé e de vivência em comunidade.

Até 11 de outubro, serão realizadas duas celebrações por dia. A Novena da Tarde acontece às 15h e a Novena Solene, às 19h. As celebrações terão a participação de bispos de diferentes regiões do país.

Novena no Santuário Nacional de Aparecida — Foto: Gustavo Marcelino/Arquivo

As reflexões da novena serão conduzidas pelo padre Ferdinando Mancilio, da Congregação do Santíssimo Redentor. Segundo o Santuário, os encontros apresentam Maria como uma discípula que soube escutar, acolher e colocar em prática a Palavra de Deus.

Além das celebrações religiosas, a programação inclui passeio ciclístico, carreata, procissão e o Festival da Padroeira.

A programação termina em 12 de outubro, quando é celebrado o Dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida. A data é feriado nacional e marca a principal celebração do ano no Santuário Nacional.

articles.title: 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' box office collection Day 1: Ajay Devgn starrer misses Rs 100 crore opening; scores Rs 95 crore global debut
articles.summary: Ajay Devgn’s ‘Drishyam 3: The Conclusion’ has made a strong start at the global box office, however, it fell short of the Rs 100 crore mark.
articles.body: Ajay Devgn’s ‘Drishyam 3: The Conclusion’ has made a strong start at the global box office, however, it fell short of the Rs 100 crore mark.According to sacnilk, the film' starring Ajay Devgn in the lead, collected Rs 66.75 crore net in India on Day 1 across 15,759 shows. Its India gross stands at Rs 80.10 crore, while the film added another Rs 15 crore gross from overseas markets, thus taking its worldwide gross to an estimated Rs 95.10 crore.The film recorded an overall 67.08% occupancy for its Hindi 2D shows. After a relatively slow start during the morning shows, the thriller witnessed an upturn in its footfalls through the day, recording its highest occupancy during the night shows at 76.46%.Drishyam 3 Movie Review‘Drishyam 3’ beats ‘Drishyam 2’ and 'Drishyam' opening‘Drishyam 3: The Conclusion’ has registered a substantially bigger opening than its predecessor, ‘Drishyam 2’. The second instalment reportedly collected Rs 15.38 crore net and Rs 18.15 crore gross in India on its opening day. Meanwhile, the first instalment of the film opened at Rs 5.85 crore net at the domestic box office.‘Drishyam 3’ marks Ajay Devgn's biggest openingThe latest film also marks the biggest opening day of Ajay Devgn’s career. As per box office reports, ‘Drishyam 3: The Conclusion’, which released on October 2, 2026, has been reported to have collected around Rs 66 crore net on its opening day. articles.title: Can big events change how a city like Southampton is seen?
articles.summary: Southampton has a packed summer calendar, with hopes of being known as a cultural destination.
articles.body:
Thousands of people have descended on Southampton for concerts, festivals and major events this summer, but can they change the way the city is seen?

From major artists performing in Guildhall Square to hundreds of musicians taking over venues across Southampton, the city has had a packed events calendar.

It comes four years after Southampton reached the final four in the race to become UK City of Culture, with council leaders subsequently pledging to build on the momentum of the bid.

So is Southampton becoming better known as a cultural destination or does it still have some way to go?

Known as the "Gateway to the World", Southampton has a longstanding connection with the maritime industry.

The Mayflower sailed from the city in 1620 before eventually crossing the Atlantic, while the Titanic departed Southampton on its ill-fated maiden voyage in 1912.

More recently, the city has become synonymous with the cruise industry, with millions of passengers passing through its port.

Those comings and goings can leave Southampton feeling like a "transient city", according to Julianne Watling-McCarthy, co-founder of Southampton Pride Trust.

The city's Pride event is free to attend and Watling-McCarthy said more than 20,000 people visited over the weekend this summer.

"Southampton isn't very good at shouting about the stuff that's great here," she said.

She added there was now "a joined-up way of working amongst cultural organisations in the city", which was largely inspired by its unsuccessful City of Culture bid.

It ultimately lost out to Bradford, but Sarah Bogle, leader of Southampton City Council and lead on growth, prosperity and culture, said the bid "provided a platform" and made the council think about "the art of the possible".

"The overall goal is to become more of a destination city and provide more experiences for people but also to help residents enjoy our city as well," she said.

Bogle said the packed summer of events was part of a conscious effort to promote Southampton.

She said analysis following Southampton Summer Sessions in June found more than 50% of visitors travelled from outside the SO postcode area.

"It's about building a brand about Southampton as a place to visit, Southampton as a place to spend time in, it's not just a place to pass through," she said.

The Southampton International Boat Show, now in its 57th year, attracted more than 91,000 visitors this year, with events director Jasmine Hill saying 70% came from outside the city.

Hill said the show reinforced Southampton as the "maritime place to go", while its work with local schools and universities aimed to "encourage the younger generation" into the industry.

But Chris Orr, event lead for Music in the City, wants people to recognise Southampton for more than its maritime heritage.

The free grassroots music event is in its 18th year and featured more than 1,800 musicians across 59 venues, with 425 live performances in a single day.

Orr said bands performing at the event had subsequently been rebooked by venues throughout the year, helping it support local talent beyond the weekend itself.

"By its nature Southampton is very spread out, there's lots of different communities and Music in the City brings them all together," he said.

As a local resident, Orr said he did not think Southampton received the recognition it deserved for its culture.

"For things like music and the arts, I don't know how recognised we are," he said.

"You often hear people quote Bristol and Brighton as music cities but I think Southampton very much is one and I think there's work to be done to get that message out there."

David McGregor, cabinet member for economy, culture, heritage and tourism at Brighton and Hove City Council, said his council treated culture like a "heritage asset" for the city.

He said economic impact studies were used to measure what events brought back to Brighton, while the council also responded to feedback and had changed or removed events when they did not feel right for the city.

McGregor acknowledged that, at a time when councils were under financial pressure, "culture and events seems like the easiest thing to cut", but said the investment was "invaluable".

He said "having an understanding of what you want to be known for" was crucial to developing a city's cultural identity.

"We have a clear understanding of the things that work and the things that don't," he said.

"Maybe that's a bit of trial and error over the years as well."

articles.title: Twisterella music festival shows Middlesbrough in 'different light'
articles.summary: Musical acts from across the world come to Middlesbrough for the Twisterella festival.
articles.body:
A music festival organiser has said he hopes to show his town "in a different light" after it recently hit the headlines.

Twisterella will see five venues in Middlesbrough host 35 acts from across the world later, including local singer Loren Heat who said it was "putting such an underestimated town on the map".

In August seven men, including two police officers, died in a head-on crash on the A66. Since then multiple people have been arrested as part of a wider police operation against organised crime in the area.

Music promoter and festival co-founder Henry Carden said after Middlesbrough fell under the spotlight for the wrong reasons, people needed to be reminded there was more to it.

He said: "I think it's a really difficult conversation because I think the things that people are seeing are happening and it's real, but there is another side to it as well.

"I think events like Twisterella and the Turner Prize coming to Mima show Middlesbrough in a different light."

He said it was a "really exciting place" to be for art, culture and music.

"There's a lot of things to shout about with a positive light on it at the moment."

Previous performers at Twisterella, now in its 12th year, have included Sam Fender and The 1975.

Among this year's acts is singer Heat, from Middlesbrough, whose career has taken her as far as Japan and Texas.

It is the third time she will play at Twisterella.

She said: "I think it's brilliant that people are out here putting such an underestimated town on the map.

"It's lovely just playing in my hometown."

Teesside University has hosted gigs as part of the festival since it started in 2014.

Head of facilities and events Luke Stretton said the festival needed to be supported, not only to bring money into the area but to keep the live music scene in the town.

He said: "We know there have been venues that have been lost over the past couple of years, venues with a real legacy like the Westgarth .

"It's important that we continue to support live music and bring live music into Middlesbrough - we need to support them here so they can get the exposure they need."

Twisterella is running throughout the day at venues across the town.

articles.title: London film festival celebrates British-Latino identity
articles.summary: The Latino film festival in the capital will screen 60 films from 27 countries over five days.
articles.body:
An event billed as London's only competitive Latino film festival is now under way for the first time in the capital.

Venues including the Barbican, the ICA, Ciné Lumière and BFI Stephen Street will screen 60 films from 27 countries until Tuesday.

There will also be workshops and performances with guests including Cuban dancer Carlos Acosta, a former principal at the Royal Ballet, Argentine actor Óscar Martínez, Cuban actor Jorge Perugorría and Oscar-winning Chilean screenwriter Gonzalo Maza.

The event was founded by Cuban actress Ketty Rodriguez who, when she moved to London, was struck by the lack of Latin representation in a city famous for its multiculturalism, film and history.

She told BBC London: "Everything here is about community, is about connection, and the idea started because I couldn't find my people, I didn't know where they were, so I decided to do this festival and it's very successful, I'm very happy."

Rodriguez says it is the first competitive Latino film festival of this size in London.

"We have received hundreds of entries from all over Latin America, and can't wait to support and showcase features, documentaries, animation, and shorts from these incredible filmmakers," she said.

Cuban dancer Javier Torres, who developed the festival idea with Rodriguez, said: "This is just the start of something great. We found a gap in the market, we found a necessity of the Latino community to come together and to give voice and narrative voices to Latin American filmmakers.

"This is a platform for diplomacy, for culture, to get together and this is what we are building here."

Alongside entries from Latin America are stories made in London for Londoners.

Victor Rios, a British-Bolivian filmmaker said the event was a chance "not just to celebrate people of Latin roots but also to celebrate British-Latino identity".

He moved to the UK at 16, and has two short films in the selection.

He said: "It's very crucial for people to understand that we are not just here passing by. We are part of society, and this festival is establishing that too.

"We're very proud to be Colombians, Bolivians, Ecuadorians, Peruvians, Chileans, but we are also British.

"So we have a place, we have a say, and we want to be heard."

The festival is backed by the BFI through National Lottery funding and by the City of London Corporation.

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Michael Douglas: ‘Whatever you do, make sure you give your best effort and try as hard as you can,’ a piece of life advice that the American actor received from his father, Kirk Douglas, about always giving 100 per cent
articles.summary: Discover the motivational wisdom of Michael Douglas as he shares life lessons from his father, Kirk Douglas. Learn about the importance of hard work and giving your best effort in everything you do. Michael Douglas's journey in Hollywood reminds us that success is built through perseverance and dedication.
articles.body: We all get told to work hard, but now and then, a piece of advice actually stays with us. Michael Douglas once shared advice that is actually quite easy to relate to. You do not always need to have everything planned out or know exactly where you are going. Sometimes, you just need to put in the effort and give whatever you are doing a proper try.Douglas has been part of Hollywood for many years, so he has seen his share of good and difficult times. He also grew up with his father, Kirk Douglas, who was already a well-known actor. Being around the film world from a young age gave Michael a close look at what it takes to build a career in the industry. So, when he talks about the value of hard work, there is a personal story behind those words.Motivational quote of the day by Michael Douglas reads, “Whatever you do, make sure you give your best effort and try as hard as you can.”What does the quote by Michael Douglas mean?Douglas was talking about his father, Kirk Douglas, when he came up with this advice. In a 2021 conversation with AARP, he was asked what the most important thing his father had taught him.At first, the quote may sound like simple advice, but there is something relatable about it. Douglas is basically saying that whatever you decide to do, give it a proper try. Things will not always turn out the way you hoped. Sometimes you put in the work and it still does not go your way. But the effort is not for nothing. You learn from what happened, figure out what you could have done differently, and take that experience with you the next time.Why Michael Douglas' message still matters today?It is hard not to compare yourself with other people these days. Social media often shows us someone's success without showing all the time, effort and failed attempts that came before it.That is where Douglas' message feels particularly relevant. Everyone has their own pace. Some goals take months to reach, while others can take years. There will also be days when things do not go as planned.Giving your best does not mean you have to be perfect every single day. Sometimes, it simply means showing up, doing what you can and trying again when something does not work out.Michael Douglas' early lifeMichael Douglas was born on September 25, 1944, in New Brunswick, New Jersey. Acting was already a familiar part of his family life. His father, Kirk Douglas, was one of Hollywood's well-known actors, while his mother, Diana Dill, also worked as an actress.Growing up with two parents from the film industry gave Douglas an early look at the world he would eventually enter himself. However, this didn't mean easy access to the world of glam or a shortcut to the industry.Douglas studied drama at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and later began looking for acting opportunities of his own. As he started taking on more roles, Michael slowly began making a name for himself instead of just being known as Kirk Douglas’ son.He had grown up around Hollywood, but building a career of his own was a different story.Michael Douglas' rise to fameMichael Douglas began getting more attention after he landed the role of Steve Keller in 'The Streets of San Francisco'. The show ran from 1972 to 1977 and became an important part of his early career.Around the same time, Douglas was also interested in what happened behind the camera. He worked as a producer on 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest' in 1976. The film went on to win the Academy Award for Best Picture.His acting career picked up even more with movies like 'Fatal Attraction', 'Wall Street' and 'Basic Instinct'. His role as Gordon Gekko in 'Wall Street' became a big moment in Michael Douglas' career as it earned him the Academy Award for Best Actor.It was just the start of his journey, as he took on all kinds of roles over the years and also spent time working as a producer. He kept trying different things and slowly built the career he became known for. Over the years, he built his career one project at a time.That makes his words about giving your best feel quite personal. He did not get where he is from one big break alone. He kept working, trying new things and moving forward. Sometimes, that really is what it comes down to — do your best and keep going.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Actress Yukti Thareja, whose credits include ‘Hai Junoon! Dream. Dare. Dominate’ and ‘Delhi Crime Season 3’, is joining ‘Farzi Season 2’ as its leading lady. Directed by the duo Raj Nidimoru and Krishna DK, the crime thriller returns next year, following a first season that made a big mark on India's OTT scene.Yukti Thareja joins the crime thrillerSpeaking to Variety India, Thareja confirmed that she is part of the show. "I'm playing the main female lead in Farzi Season 2. I'm the only central female protagonist this season. All my scenes are with Shahid Kapoor. My character is a fearless Gen-Z woman who speaks up against the system. It's a strong, layered role with real substance. I've already shot the majority of my portion, with about 20% left to complete, and the season is expected to release in mid-2027."Yukti Thareja enters Sunny and Firoz's worldIn the first season of ‘Farzi’, Kapoor played Sunny, a restless young man who turns to forging currency. It closed with Sunny and his best friend Firoz (Bhuvan Arora) slipping away from both Special Task Force officer Michael Vedanayagam (Vijay Sethupathi) and crime lord Mansoor Dalal (Kay Kay Menon). Season two will follow the pair as they keep their counterfeiting operation running while staying one step ahead of these two dangerous adversaries.Yukti Thareja's rise from 'Lut Gaye' to 'Marco'Thareja rose to popularity through the music video ‘Lut Gaye’, where she appeared opposite Emraan Hashmi. articles.title: 'Mirzapur: The Movie' director Gurmmeet Singh, says Jitendra Kumar replacing Vikrant Massey as Bablu Pandit was 'blessing in disguise'
articles.summary: Director Gurmmeet Singh has spoken about one of the biggest changes in 'Mirzapur: The Movie', the casting of Jitendra Kumar as Bablu Pandit in place of
articles.body: Director Gurmmeet Singh has spoken about one of the biggest changes in 'Mirzapur: The Movie', the casting of Jitendra Kumar as Bablu Pandit in place of Vikrant Massey. In a chat with, he explained how the decision shaped the film and the character.Why Jitendra Kumar stepped in as Bablu PanditThe film revisits the world and characters introduced in the first season of the series. In that season, Vikrant Massey played Bablu, the younger brother of Guddu Pandit. In the film, the role is played by Jitendra Kumar.Talking about the change, Gurmmeet Singh said, "I think the beauty about a make-believe world or doing something creative and fiction is that as an artiste, one always needs to have choices, right? As creators, as actors, what's the one thing that we all desperately want? It's to have choices and to be able to make that choice. And it's a good lesson to learn that everyone needs to be able to follow what their heart is telling them to do. No story, no character, no journey is bound down by anybody, right? The show will always move forward, and that's the beauty we can take forward from this, that with Jitendra coming in, it brought a new energy into the show. It also gave the film its own identity."A bigger and bolder BabluThe director said the new casting also let the team rethink the character and give him a more important place in the story.He said, "It gave it its own life, which is very different from the show, which is what we always wanted anyways. So it became a blessing in disguise. We were able to reimagine Bablu and give him more agency. The Bablu in the show was almost aiding his brother and was a victim, never having agency or an agenda of his own. But this Bablu is playing the game. He's the one driving the narrative."Turning a setback into a lessonGurmmeet also shared what the team learnt from the experience. "So, I think that's a great learning we've taken away, to always use your setbacks to your advantage, because that's what creativity is meant to do. Look ahead, and with the film doing as well as it has, I think it only opens up so many doors for us."Film continues its strong run'Mirzapur: The Movie' is doing well at the box office. On Day 27, its worldwide gross stands at Rs 333.29 crore. Amid this success, Gurmmeet opened up about the creative choices behind the film and how the characters have grown over the years.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Arde Bogotá: "Nos llevaríamos de gira a Borja Iglesias y también pondríamos en la percusión a Cucurella"
articles.standfirst: La banda de Cartagena presenta nuevo álbum con su gira de los 'Hervideros' en 'sold out'
articles.summary: La banda de Cartagena presenta nuevo álbum con su gira de los 'Hervideros' en 'sold out'
articles.body: Hay bandas que nacen con la intención de hacer ruido y otras que, casi sin darse cuenta, terminan convirtiéndose en el ruido que todo el mundo escucha. Arde Bogotá pertenece a ese segundo grupo. Cuatro músicos de Cartagena que comenzaron a tocar juntos en 2017, que debutaron en 2021 con 'La noche' y que dos años después, con 'Cowboys de la A3', dieron el salto que cambió para siempre la dimensión del proyecto. Aquel segundo álbum convirtió a la banda en uno de los grandes nombres del rock español, con una gira de más de 150 conciertos, discos de oro y platino y dos nominaciones a los Grammy Latinos. Desde entonces, Arde Bogotá ha vivido esa situación extraña en la que una banda deja de ser una promesa para convertirse en una referencia y empieza a tener que convivir con las expectativas que genera. Ellos mismos reconocen que una de las preguntas que más les rondaba antes de publicar su nuevo trabajo era precisamente qué ocurriría cuando, después de tres años y medio sin un álbum, las canciones dejaran de pertenecerles únicamente a ellos. "Pues que no le guste a nadie", responde Pepe cuando le preguntamos qué es lo que más miedo les da. Este viernes, ese momento llegó. Arde Bogotá publicó 'Manufacturas del Club de la Gente Sola', su tercer álbum de estudio, un trabajo construido durante meses entre Cartagena y Los Ángeles y producido por Joe Chiccarelli. Once canciones que nacen de un proceso colectivo en el que las ideas se destripan entre los cuatro hasta convertirlas en algo que todos quieran defender. Incluso el título tuvo que sobrevivir a una lista de unos 400 nombres antes de acabar imponiéndose el de esa empresa ficticia que, dentro del universo del disco, fabrica corazones que no sienten. Pero la publicación del disco llega después de un capítulo especialmente intenso para la banda: los 'Hervideros'. Una serie de conciertos con entradas físicas que agotó sus diez fechas y provocó largas colas, incluyendo personas que pasaron la noche esperando para conseguir una entrada. Una decisión que Arde Bogotá defiende, aunque Antonio reconoce que hubo momentos de vértigo al comprobar hasta dónde podía llegar la respuesta del público. "Hay cosas que escapan a tu control y da miedo que alguien pueda hacerse daño o pasarlo mal", explica. Ahora, con el nuevo disco ya fuera de la fábrica y una gira más grande en el horizonte, Arde Bogotá afronta la etapa más ambiciosa de su carrera. Hablan de los escenarios que todavía sueñan con pisar, de lo que significa que les reconozcan en el supermercado, de las cosas que no soportan de sus compañeros, del boxeo de Jota, de fútbol, de política, de los nervios de tocar en Cibeles y de aquello que todavía les queda por conseguir. Porque, después de haber convertido una banda nacida en Cartagena en uno de los grandes fenómenos del rock español, el siguiente paso ya no parece consistir únicamente en llegar más lejos, sino en decidir hasta dónde quieren llegar. Pregunta: ¿Qué es lo que más miedo os da después de estar tres años y medio sin sacar algo? Pepe: Pues que no le guste a nadie. Antonio: Que nos digan: ‘Para hacer esto...’. Jota: A nosotros nos gusta, pero ya, claro. P: ¿Cómo es el proceso para componer y cuánto de democrático del grupo es el proceso a la hora de elegir qué canciones metéis en el álbum? Antonio: El proceso de alguien viene con una idea y entre todos se destripa, se trabaja siempre y hasta que se convierta en algo que nos guste. Y luego meter en el álbum no ha sido democrático, ha sido consenso. O estábamos todos de acuerdo o no lo vamos a hacer. No tendría sentido tener algo en el álbum que alguien no quiera tener o que no le guste o que no quiera defenderlo. P: Tuvisteis sobre la mesa 400 títulos para el álbum, ¿cómo acabasteis eligiendo ‘Manufacturas del Club de la Gente Sola’? Antonio: Fue también consenso. Es verdad que había varias formas de referirnos al proyecto y al final ganó la que más tiempo llevaba porque ese nombre estaba ya en el archivo inicial del ordenador con el que empezó todo. Ya estaba la idea de que esto fuera como una especie de empresa ficticia que fabrica un corazón que no siente. Y el nombre de la empresa era este: ‘Manufacturas del Club de la Gente Sola’. Y al final nos quedamos con ese. P: ¿Cuál es el peor consejo que os han dado en el mundo de la música? Pepe: Dibuja menos y limítate a hacer la base. Antonio: Mi amigo Paco me dijo: ‘Antonio, las camisas esas que te pones... No, nada, tío’. Y yo pensé: SÍ. Dani: Compra un Kemper (risas). Jota: No sé, no tengo malos consejos. P: Dani y Antonio, os conocisteis discutiendo sobre si el rock había muerto, ahora que sois una de las bandas con más éxito de España, ¿quién tenía razón aquella noche? Dani: Bueno, quizá más que si había muerto el rock, era qué era el rock en español. Y qué había ahí dentro. Y cómo la gente en nuestro país concebía ese concepto. Creo que después de un tiempo y de haber pasado nosotros y muchos compañeros dentro de ese concepto, a día de hoy, creo que cada vez cabe más gente. Que abras una playlist de Spotify y estemos nosotros y estén los compañeros de Niña Polaca, Ultraligera, Carlos Ares y también esté Marea, Extremoduro y muchas bandas históricas es una buena noticia. P: ¿Quién fue el primero en dejar su trabajo para apostar por la música? Antonio: Yo creo que el primero que abandonó todo fue Pepe o Dani. Pepe: Sí, yo fui el primero que me quedé sin trabajo, más que abandonarlo. Creo que me echaron por tener que pedir los fines de semana para irme a tocar. Y creo que el último. Creo que fuiste tú (señala a Antonio). P: ¿Y cómo se toma esa decisión? Pepe: ¿Obligatoriamente? Antonio: Al Pepe no le quedó otra (risas). Yo cuando hubo dinero para pagarme el alquiler. Cuando la banda dijo: da para repartiros 400 euros al mes para cada uno y dije: con eso me quedo. Es lo que pago de alquiler. P: ¿Qué consejo con lo que sabéis hoy le daríais a los Arde Bogotá que hacían sus primeras maquetas? Antonio: Guau. Quizás lo animaría a escuchar más música. Le empujaría a tocar más, estudiar más. Creo que eso es lo que te da herramientas para crear más. P: ¿Qué tiene la Región de Murcia para que se haya convertido en uno de los grandes centros de la música nacional? Dani: Que tiene una ciudad increíble como Cartagena (risas). Antonio: Buena gente, supongo, porque la mayoría, el 99% de la gente que está en la música en la Región de Murcia es muy buena gente. Pepe: Hay una escena. Jota: Hay muchas bandas, hay muchos locales para tocar. Depende de dónde mires, porque en la ciudad de Murcia, por ejemplo, tienen muchos locales para tocar, muchas salas de ensayo. No es que haya una escena claramente definida porque hay microescenas. Pero es verdad que tú lo ves y sabes que hay un cúmulo de distintos espacios de creación, hay muchos blogs, muchos medios que se involucran en la música, hay festivales... P: No erais amigos antes de formar el grupo, ahora que ya lleváis tiempo trabajando juntos... ¿Qué es lo que no soportáis los unos de los otros? Antonio: Si queréis podemos decir qué creemos que los demás no soportan de uno mismo mejor mejor que echarle mierda a los demás. Que ya nos la hemos echado, pero para no reavivar conversaciones que ya hemos zanjado. Yo creo que no soportan mi mal humor. Es que tengo un mal humor muy malo y muchas veces cuando estoy cansado respondo fatal. Soy muy serio y muy tajante. Jota: Yo voy a decir dos cosas: una, que me quejo demasiado en general, sobre todo de enfermedades, que también te digo que quejarse gratis, entonces pedalea (hace una peineta), y la otra es esto que acaba de ocurrir, que ha sido sin querer, que a veces mis maneras son un poco toscas, no me soporto ni yo. Dani: Esto es algo que ya me han dicho... que cuando algo no me mola se me nota. Jota: ¡Que casualmente pasa cada vez que nos mira! (risas) Pepe: Uf, yo peco de quejarme, creo que se me nota que no me gustan las cosas, también llego tarde, no afino, soy dramático... Antonio: Yo diría que lo de llegar tarde, sobre todo cuando dices: chicos, tengo dos retrasos, el mío y otro de 15 minutos (risas). Pepe: ¿Pero eso lo odiáis? Dani: Lo que odiamos es que lo digas cuando ya estamos abajo (risas). P: ¿Alguna vez habéis usado vuestra fama para pedir mesa en un restaurante o entrar en algún sitio? Antonio: Yo no, pero unos amigos lo usaron una vez en mi nombre para ir a una discoteca. Dijeron: “vamos con el cantante de Arde Bogotá”. Creo que les preguntaron: “¿Quién es ese?”. Lo buscaron en Google (risas). P: Habéis agotado las entradas para la gira de Los Hervideros en tiempo récord, ¿os habéis arrepentido en algún momento de hacer este formato? Antonio: Yo sí he tenido vértigo de haber hecho las entradas físicas. Hubo gente que pasó la noche fuera, gente mayor, niños y era como: “hostia”. Todo estuvo todo lo controlado que pudimos pero hay cosas que escapan a tu control y da miedo que alguien pueda hacerse daño o pasarlo mal. P: De todos modos en 2027 habrá una gira más grande... Antonio: Sí, claro. Intentamos comunicar todo con sentido común y decir: “vamos a hacer una gira más grande a la que esperamos que venga todo el mundo”. Esto es solo una presentación. Aún así sigo pensando que era la mejor opción, no me arrepiento. Jota: Es una parte interesante del público, del ser humano, de cómo funciona. Si lo consigues bien, si no lo consigues: ‘vaya mierda’. Es así siempre. Y nosotros hemos intentado ir a todos los sitios posibles. Lo que pasa es que no todas las salas permitían hacer el formato de hervidero. Hay una serie de cosas positivas y una serie de comentarios de los que se puede aprender para mejorar la experiencia del usuario para la venta. P: Claro, antes la gente hacía cola durante horas y se quedaba sin entradas y no pasaba nada... Antonio: Antes no existía Twitter. Entonces cuando tú estabas frustrado, me imagino que le pegabas a un contenedor y ahora tienes Twitter. Han salido ganando las empresas de contenedores, pero quizás era más efectivo eso. P: Para la gira de 2027, ¿qué podemos esperar? ¿Más ciudades, sitios más grandes o ambas? Antonio: Ambas. Estamos trabajando en ello ahora mismo pero sí, el objetivo es intentar ir a todos los sitios que podamos y tratar de hacer algo emocionante, aunque no sea tan condensado como un hervidero, pero sí algo emocionante. P. ¿Cuál es el recinto de España que os hace pensar: “Algún día tenemos que tocar ahí”? Jota. En algún sitio icónico como San Mamés. Antonio. El Metropolitano. Pepe. El Cartagonova. Dani. Hay un sitio en el que no hemos estado y me da rabia: la Wurli (Wurlitzer Ballroom). Y veo dificil que podamos tocar algún allí porque es un sitio muy pequeño. P: Habéis tocado para en la celebración del Mundial en Cibeles. ¿Hay algo diferente entre tocar delante de ese público, de un aficionado a tocar delante de vuestros fans? Antonio: Sí, sí, la gente que vino a las celebraciones Cibeles quería celebrar que se había ganado el campeonato del Mundo de fútbol. Y nosotros somos parte del evento. Pero a lo mejor no nos conocen o no les gusta lo que hacemos. Pero bueno, estuvimos allí para apoyar y ya. P: ¿Visteis la final del Mundial? Antonio: Claro, claro que sí. Es el partido en el que más nervioso he estado de nuestra vida, yo creo, porque sabíamos que si ganábamos nos íbamos a las ocho a Madrid. Entonces te juegas varias cosas. De repente es el nervio de tener que subir a Cibeles a cantar. P: O sea que ya sabían avisado con antelación. Dani: Un día antes, no te creas que mucho antes... Antonio: A partir de la semifinal o así ya empieza como a gestarse el evento. Jota: Sobre todo por la logística del asunto. Nosotros incidimos en que queríamos tocar sí o sí en directo, ni playback, ni medio playback, ni ‘candemor’, solo riguroso directo y la verdad es que aceptaron, con lo que lo complicado es la logística, con todos los jugadores en el escenario y tal. Dani: Imagínate el partido: no, se anula el gol y todo el mundo: no vas a tocar. ¿Me hago la maleta? No me hago la maleta... P: ¿Si tuvierais que llevar a un futbolista de gira a quién sería? Todos: A Borja Iglesias. Antonio: Que cargue algún cable también, que está muy fuerte el tío. Pregunta: ¿Y si tuvierais que escoger a uno como miembro de la banda? Pepe: Cucurella, percusionista. Jota: Se le ve que el zagal tiene azogue. Entonces yo creo que darle una percusión... Antonio: Aprendería, aprendería rápido. Pregunta: Como forofos del Atleti... ¿Se merece Julián Álvarez el perdón de los aficionados? Antonio: Guau. Yo soy muy propenso a perdonar, me educaron en eso. Entonces yo podría llegar a perdonarlo. Pepe: Creo que tiene que trabajar en ello, pero se puede perdonar. Pregunta: Jota, tú haces boxeo... ¿No tenéis una cláusula de prohibición de actividades de riesgo? Jota: Esto es un problema, pero como yo en mi vida es muy probable que acabe lesionado o me rompa algo, vivimos con ello. No es la primera vez que tengo que tocar con piedras en el riñón, me he hecho en el tobillo un esguince de grado tres y se ha tocado, no pasa nada. Dani: ¿Pero compites? Jota: Yo hago sparring, pero te pegas. Lo que pasa es que me pego con casco y con bucal. Normalmente controlas la fuerza, pero notas que te meten una guantá, te mosqueas y empiezas a dar. No da miedo, solo cuando hay cosas de promo que digo: ‘¿Podéis no darme aquí?’ (se señala la cara). Antonio: Si no es lo más peligroso que hacen miembros de esta banda... Aquí hay gente que tira tabiques con las manos y luego tienen que tocar instrumentos. Dani: Lo dicen porque me hice la propia demolición de mi casa, de la reforma de mi casa. (risas) Y además vivía en ella. Acabé yendo al hospital porque tenía los pulmones negros y escupía negro. Me dijeron: “O es un cáncer o tienes polvo”. Pues va a ser eso porque hoy he tirado el cuarto de baño... P: Hablemos de actualidad: Ceuta, desahucios, guerras internacionales, políticos corruptos... ¿Cómo ves el panorama ahora mismo de la actualidad? Antonio: Si lo pintas así, fatal, la verdad. Creo que vivimos un momento complejo de la historia de nuestro país pero no por eso tiene que ser un momento desalentador, ¿no? Quizás se trata de un momento para que, como ciudadanos, hagamos reflexiones respecto de la inmigración, respecto del derecho a la vivienda, respecto de la gente que nos representa en la política actual y actuemos en consecuencia. Quizás salga algo positivo y se encuentren respuestas para problemas que parecían irresolubles. P: Para terminar, le hemos preguntado a la Inteligencia Artificial qué os preguntaría si solo pudiera haceros una sola pregunta y nos ha dicho esto: ¿Qué canción de las que aún no habéis escrito sabéis que necesitáis componer para dar el siguiente paso? ¿Qué tema os da pánico tocar en ella? Antonio: ¡Guau! ¡Qué buena pregunta! ¡Qué tema nos da pánico tocar! Pepe: Un villancico. Como la mujer que cada año sale en Navidad (Mariah Carey). Antonio: Es la canción que aún no hemos hecho con una temática que nos da pánico tocar, que es el nacimiento de Cristo. Jota: Además de que se nos pidió cantar villancicos fuera de temporada. Antonio: A mí me parece que da mala suerte. Entonces, si solo podemos grabar villancicos e interpretarlos en diciembre, sería muy complejo...

articles.summary: Nani and director Srikanth Odela’s latest action thriller ‘The Paradise’ is in its second weekend with the film crossing Rs 110 crore total India net and
articles.body: Nani and director Srikanth Odela’s latest action thriller ‘The Paradise’ is in its second weekend with the film crossing Rs 110 crore total India net and Rs 160 crore mark worldwide. As the film saw a strong opening during its first weekend, later it lost its momentum facing criticism and mixed reviews from the audience.‘The Paradise’ enters its second weekendThe Nani-led film has also continued to earn from overseas markets. On second Friday, it added approximately Rs. 10 lakh to its overseas gross, taking the cumulative overseas collection to Rs. 30.95 crore. articles.summary: Bollywood stars are saluting the courage of Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who helped save 174 people on a Flydubai flight after being stabbed by
articles.body: Bollywood stars are saluting the courage of Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who helped save 174 people on a Flydubai flight after being stabbed by his co-pilot in mid-air. After Salman Khan, Shah Rukh Khan has now posted a message of praise for the pilot on social media.Shah Rukh Khan's message for the captainShah Rukh Khan wrote on X, "Captain Smit Machchhar, you stood strong when it mattered the most!! It's not easy to stare adversity in the face and put one's safety on the line… but you did just that to protect those onboard and showed us what being a Captain entails. A true display of courage and duty. Wishing you a speedy recovery, the country is proud of you…"Salman Khan's note a day earlierShah Rukh Khan's post came a day after Salman Khan also praised the pilot. On Friday night, Salman wrote on X, "Kamaal kar diya pilot ji, hum sab aap ko salute karte hain (You've done a fantastic job, Pilot-ji; we all salute you) Will be a pleasure to fly with u.. Well done bro.. Capt #SmitMachchhar."Karan Johar, Ranveer Singh and others join inMany other film personalities have also spoken up. Karan Johar shared the captain's photo and wrote, "It takes another grain of courage to be fighting for your own life but in that split second, put the lives of all others before yours. And that's what captain Smit Machchhar did in the face of the toughest times. And for that, the entire country & humankind is behind you! Thank you for your selfless, courageous and brave heart, you are an inspiration for the generations to come."Vicky Kaushal called the pilot a "braveheart", while Ranveer Singh described him as "courageous". Paresh Rawal, R Madhavan, Vijay Deverakonda and Ravi Kishan also praised him and wished him a quick recovery.What happened on the Flydubai flight?Captain Smit Machchhar was flying Flydubai flight FZ1073, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 going from Dubai to Tel Aviv. There were 174 people on board, including 27 children. On September 30, while the plane was over Saudi Arabia, his co-pilot attacked and stabbed him inside the cockpit.Even though he was badly hurt, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door. This let passengers and crew step in and overpower the attacker. Two other pilots who were travelling on the flight then took charge of the aircraft. It was diverted and landed safely at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia.Captain Smit Machchhar speaks to PM ModiSmit Machchhar was taken to hospital after the incident. He later spoke to Prime Minister Narendra Modi from his hospital bed. During the call, he described how he opened the cockpit door despite his injuries, which helped others stop the attacker and kept the passengers safe from further danger.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: La actriz acudió al desfile de Messika con un diseño negro de Roberto Cavalli que combinó con joyas de diamantes de la firma francesa
articles.body: Ester Expósito ha vuelto a convertirse en uno de los rostros más destacados de la Semana de la Moda de París. La actriz acudió al desfile de Messika con un espectacular vestido negro de Roberto Cavalli que dejó gran parte de su espalda al descubierto y que destaca por su combinación de seda, transparencias y volantes. El diseño, que forma parte de la colección otoño-invierno 2026/27 de la firma italiana, tiene un precio de 2.500 euros. La intérprete apostó por un estilismo en el que el vestido concentraba prácticamente toda la atención. Se trata de una pieza larga confeccionada en seda, con escote pronunciado en forma de V, tirantes muy finos y mangas caídas que dejan los hombros al aire. La silueta fluida aporta movimiento al conjunto, mientras que los diferentes volantes recorren parte de la falda. Pero el detalle más llamativo aparece al girarse. La parte posterior del vestido queda prácticamente abierta por completo, con el tejido cayendo desde los tirantes y dejando la espalda al descubierto. Las transparencias del material añaden además un efecto lencero al conjunto sin necesidad de incorporar más elementos. Para completar el estilismo, Expósito recurrió a varias piezas de joyería de Messika. Un collar de diamantes y unos pendientes aportaron el toque de brillo sobre el vestido negro y reforzaron el carácter sofisticado de su aparición en el desfile. La actriz optó también por llevar el cabello recogido en una coleta baja, dejando algunos mechones sueltos alrededor del rostro. El maquillaje, natural y luminoso, mantuvo el protagonismo en el vestido y las joyas. Su aparición en el desfile de Messika vuelve a situarla entre las invitadas que más atención han generado durante estos días de moda en París. Una elección que combina una de las tendencias más presentes en las propuestas de noche, como las transparencias, con el diseño clásico de un vestido negro y el sello de Roberto Cavalli.

articles.title: Prince William, Kate Middleton’s secret nicknames exposed as former staffer reveals palace WhatsApp habits
articles.summary: Royal family WhatsApp nicknames exposed by a former staffer, from Prince William's "Bobcat" to Prince Harry's "Baz" and other secret aliases.
articles.body: Behind palace doors, it's apparently less "Your Royal Highness" and more "Bobcat." A former royal staffer is pulling back the curtain on Prince William and Kate Middleton's reported WhatsApp nicknames. Jack Stooks, who worked for King Charles for 21 years as a gardener at Highgrove, shared a rare glimpse into how members of the royal family reportedly identified one another on the messaging app. "I remember Princes William and Harry always had the latest phones," Stooks explained to GB News. "They actually gave their numbers out to staff so we could contact them about logistical things. They also had our numbers, and they would just WhatsApp us if they needed anything." PRINCE WILLIAM AND KATE MIDDLETON’S ‘GENUINE LOVE STORY' IS BUILT ON BEING A 'VERY NORMAL FAMILY': AUTHOR "We couldn't have them saved under their real names, so they had nicknames instead," said Stooks. "William was 'Bobcat', Harry was 'Baz', and when Catherine joined the family, she became ‘Mrs. Bobcat.’" Stooks told Fox News Digital on behalf of OLBG that only a limited number of staff were given the royals' phone numbers, which had to be kept a closely guarded secret. "We had the family under different names, so that if anyone's phone was taken, the number could be differentiated," he explained. "That way, no one knew which number was which. They all change their numbers regularly, so I don't have any of their phone numbers now." WATCH: ROYAL FAMILY'S CHEEKY NICKNAMES FOR EACH OTHER REVEALED "The nickname I gave to Harry on my phone was ‘Baz,’" Stooks shared. "He was always called ‘Baz’ by his friends, so I just took that. From memory, William was ‘Wombat,’ again because that is what his friends called him." Fox News Digital reached out to Buckingham Palace and Kensington Palace for comment. Stooks told GB News that the royal family "are big WhatsApp users." "He may have a lot of privilege, but William was never one to demand something from staff," Stooks told the outlet. "He was really polite. He would always check how busy I was before asking me to do errands for him. And whenever I said I would do something for William, he would always reply: 'You're a legend.'" "They have groups with their friends, and there is also a family group with the royal cousins, including Prince William, Zara Tindall, Peter Phillips and the York sisters," he continued. "They're very much like any other family when it comes to keeping in touch through their phones." Several royal experts told Fox News Digital that members of the royal family have long used nicknames. Some are terms of affection, while others have reportedly been used as aliases for privacy or security. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "When they had a security issue, William and Kate are known as Danny Collins and Daphne Clark, DC," royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital. "In other words, Duke and Duchess of Cambridge," he said, referring to the Prince and Princess of Wales. "The late queen was always known as Sharon, believe it or not, just for the simple S, which stood for sovereign." "King Charles and Queen Camilla, do they call themselves that? No," said Turner. "They call themselves Fred and Gladys. Why? Because in the 1950s and 1960s, Prince Charles used to listen to a radio show each week called 'The Goon Show,' which was a comedy show where Fred and Gladys were called. When he started a romance with Queen Camilla, the joke started as well. That's where Fred and Gladys first started." "And then you would think, why on earth would the queen, Elizabeth that is, be called any other nickname other than Your Majesty?" he said. "Prince Philip used to call the queen Cabbage." British broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that the name derived from the French "mon petit chou," or "my little cabbage." "I believe he also affectionately called her sausage," Chard added. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "When Prince William, as a little boy, fell at Buckingham Palace, he was overheard by a guest crying out, 'Gary! Gary!’" said British royals expert Hilary Fordwich. "The Queen told the surprised guest, 'I'm Gary. He hasn't learned to say "Granny" yet.'" Several royal experts noted that at university, William was known as "Steve" in an attempt to fly under the radar. One of the royal family's best-known nicknames is "Lilibet." Then-Princess Elizabeth struggled to pronounce her own name as a toddler, and her grandfather, King George V, reportedly imitated her pronunciation. Her husband, Prince Philip, also affectionately called her "Lilibet," and the name was later chosen by Prince Harry and Meghan Markle for their daughter, Princess Lilibet. But not all royal nicknames were affectionate. "Courtiers have long referred to Prince Harry and the former Prince Andrew, as the 'Dukes of Hazard,' which needs no explanation," said Fordwich. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "When Kate is getting a little bit upset with William in any way, she starts using the names of 'Baldy' and ‘Big Willy,'" Turner alleged, a claim previously made by author Tom Quinn. A Kensington Palace spokesperson previously told Fox News Digital that the palace doesn't comment on books. King Charles has reportedly used other terms of affection for Queen Camilla. "Back in 2022, the king was heard at an event referring to Camilla as 'Mehbooba,' the Urdu word for 'my beloved,'" said Fordwich. Charles has publicly used the term for Camilla. While still Prince of Wales, he referred to her as "my mehbooba" during a British Asian Trust speech. "Princess Diana's family always referred to her as 'Dutch,' short for 'Duchess.' She wasn't an actual duchess, but her family gave it to her as she had always behaved that way as a young girl. Her nickname for her brother, Charles Spencer, was 'Carlos,'" Fordwich said. Charles Spencer has also spoken about the siblings' nicknames. In a September interview, he said their stepfather began calling Diana "the Duchess" because she had a "very refined air," which the family shortened to "Dutch." Spencer also said Diana called him "Carlos." During the film’s promotions, the couple spoke about celebrations, making memories and how their outlook on life has changed.Rashmika Mandanna says Vijay Deverakonda needs to celebrate moreIn a conversation with YouTube channel Sudhir Srinivasan, the couple was asked whether ‘Ranabaali’ was a milestone for them as their first film together after marriage.Vijay said, “I don't even know if I believe in things like milestones and stuff.”When asked whether he was someone who did not celebrate monthly anniversaries, Rashmika Mandanna replied, “He doesn't celebrate anything.”Rashmika Mandanna explained that she believes in celebrating even the smallest moments in life. That's my approach to life every day I wake up is like war, it's like survival and that's how I talk, that's how I behave so for me celebration is like, celebrating what there's so much to do. articles.title: 'Digger' Review: Tom Cruise destroys the planet in Alejandro Iñárritu's grandiose, messy political satire
articles.summary: Fox News Digital reviews Warner Bros. Pictures' "Digger" starring Tom Cruise, John Goodman, Riz Ahmed, Sandra Hüller and Jesse Plemons. Directed by Alejandro Iñárritu.
articles.body: A great satire must be two things: innovative and funny. Unfortunately for Tom Cruise and Oscar-winning director Alejandro G. Iñárritu, "Digger" is neither of those things. Cruise is nearly unrecognizable, buried under layers upon layers of prosthetics transforming himself into Digger Rockwell, an eccentric oil tycoon who has affection for his wealth and his chronically ill robotic-like cat Maggie. Digger doesn't like to take no for an answer, even as he's repeatedly warned that a crack at his oil drilling site in Greenland could lead to catastrophe. ‘PRIMETIME’ REVIEW: ROBERT PATTINSON CHANNELS CHRIS HANSEN IN RIVETING DRAMATIZATION OF ‘TO CATCH A PREDATOR’ Well, catastrophe quickly takes shape — what started as a small crack turned into an explosion seemingly in the blink of an eye, causing a massive ice shelf to break off and head straight to Europe. The worst fears of a tsunami and mass flooding impacting tens of millions of Europeans may become a reality. The international dilemma puts Digger in the crosshairs — with President Compson (John Goodman) and his evangelical cabinet rushing to his remote taxidermy-filled estate to do damage control. ‘RESIDENT EVIL’ REVIEW: DIRECTOR ZACH CREGGER DELIVERS INFECTIOUS REBOOT TO GORY VIDEO GAME FRANCHISE What's frustrating about "Digger" is that it has all the pieces of a great film. As much as there is to admire Cruise as an actor, his performance here feels like a mishmash of his past performances (see Les Grossman in "Tropic Thunder," or Frank T.J. Mackey in "Magnolia"). This has been positioned as the role that could finally earn him a competitive Oscar, but he and the rest of the top-tier cast give one-note performances, most of which involve yelling hysterically. 'THE DOG STARS' REVIEW: JACOB ELORDI FIGHTS FOR SURVIVAL IN RIDLEY SCOTT'S DULL POST-APOCALYPTIC WESTERN Goodman's Compson clearly borrows elements from Donald Trump, but love or hate Trump, at least he's a nuanced man. Oscar-nominated German actress Sandra Hüller ("Anatomy of a Fall," "Project Hail Mary") is utterly wasted playing Digger's half sister Emma, spending all her screen time complaining how Digger's global disaster will negatively impact her environmental non-profit (which he funds anyway). The only cast member who remotely gives a compelling performance is Riz Ahmed, who plays the soft-spoken scientist who has been sounding the alarm about the consequences of Rockwell Corp's costly drilling. Iñárritu, who directed and co-wrote 2014's Best Picture winner "Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance)" — an actual great satire about showbiz — attempts to swing big here but ultimately strikes out. Unlike "Birdman," the laughs here are few and far between. Iñárritu takes bold narrative risks with plot twists that are commendable, yet there isn't enough for an audience to engage with. "Digger" clearly tries to emulate Stanley Kubrick's 1964 Oscar-nominated classic "Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb," which is regarded as one of the greatest movie satires of all time. Instead, it's more like 2021's "Don't Look Up," the insufferable satire from Adam McKay that's a giant metaphor for climate change (of course, the Academy gave it a Best Picture nod). Both sacrifice humor for over-the-top preachiness. The most redeeming aspect of "Digger" is that it was still incredibly well-crafted between the stunning visuals from Oscar-winning cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki and the whimsical score from Cosmo Sheldrake. BOX OFFICE COMEBACK: HOW SUMMER 2026 OFFERS A GLIMMER OF HOPE FOR HOLLYWOOD IN THE POST-COVID ERA CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS The Verdict Despite Cruise and Iñárritu's best efforts, "Digger" is truly a mess of a film that's unworthy of the work we're used to seeing from the two of them. You're better off revisiting "Dr. Strangelove," "Birdman" or any Cruise classic. It's easily the biggest misfire of awards season. ★★ — SKIP IT "Digger" is rated R for pervasive language.
