articles.summary: Bob Hope's unconventional Palm Springs residence, dubbed the 'UFO House', originally listed for $50 million, eventually sold for $13 million in 2016 after years on the market. Discover the unique design and history behind this architectural gem.
articles.body: When Bob Hope’s unusual Palm Springs residence appeared on the property market in 2013, its $50 million price tag immediately grabbed attention. The house was already famous for its futuristic appearance, unusual architecture and connection to one of Hollywood’s best-known entertainers. Yet, despite its history and distinctive design, the property did not find a buyer at the original asking price.After several years on the market and a major reduction in its price, the estate was eventually sold for $13 million in 2016.The story of the property, including details of its original listing and eventual sale, was documented by TopTenRealEstateDeals.com.Bob Hope’s unusual Palm Springs retreatThe home was created for Bob Hope and his wife, Dolores, by celebrated architect John Lautner. Construction of the Palm Springs property was completed in the 1970s, with its dramatic design making it very different from the traditional homes associated with Hollywood celebrities.Lautner created a structure dominated by sweeping curves, concrete surfaces and large areas of glass. The home’s huge, curved roof is probably what catches the eye first, giving the house a look that feels completely different from the homes around it.Lautner had originally imagined the design to resemble a volcano. But because of its unusual shape, people eventually started comparing it to a flying saucer, which is how the house picked up its well-known nickname, the ‘UFO House.’The house also sits beautifully against the Palm Springs desert. Its large windows let in plenty of sunlight while giving the people inside wide views of the mountains and the surrounding landscape.There was also an unusual feature inside the house. Openings in parts of the roof allowed the residents to look directly toward the sky, adding another element to Lautner’s experimental approach to the design.A celebrity estate unlike the usual mansionThe property was enormous, covering approximately 23,000 square feet. Its size, however, was only one part of what made the residence unusual.The home had several bedrooms and bathrooms, along with plenty of room for guests to relax and spend time together. There were swimming pools, a spa, a pond and a tennis court, giving the property many of the amenities expected from a luxury celebrity residence.But unlike many large Hollywood homes, the house was not designed simply to impress through size and decoration. Its architecture was the main attraction.Lautner combined concrete, glass and steel beneath the expansive roof to create a structure that blended into the desert while still appearing futuristic. The open spaces and curved forms also reflected the architect’s interest in creating homes that interacted with their surroundings.For Bob Hope, the residence became one of Palm Springs' most recognisable private properties.The $50 million listing that struggled to find a buyerThe estate went up for sale in 2013, around a decade after Bob Hope's passing in 2003. At the time, the asking price was an eye-catching $50 million.However, the property did not attract a buyer willing to pay that amount. The price was eventually reduced to approximately $24.999 million, but the home continued to remain on the market.Its unusual architecture may have made it highly recognisable, but that same individuality also meant it was not an ordinary luxury property. A house of that size, design and history required a buyer who appreciated its architectural significance as well as its celebrity connection.After spending years looking for a new owner, the property finally found one.Ronald Burkle bought the home for $13 millionIn 2016, billionaire investor and philanthropist Ronald Burkle purchased Bob Hope’s Palm Springs estate for $13 million.The final price was considerably lower than the $50 million figure attached to the home when it first entered the market. The sale therefore became an interesting chapter in the property's history, particularly because of the gap between its original asking price and eventual selling price.Burkle was known for his interest in important properties and architecture.A home that still gets attentionEven today, Bob Hope’s Palm Springs house stands out. It carries the memory of the comedian who once lived there, but much of its appeal also comes from John Lautner’s unusual design. The house feels very different from a typical celebrity mansion, which is perhaps why people still talk about it.The property also went through quite a change before finding a new owner. It was put on the market for $50 million in 2013 and was eventually sold for $13 million in 2016. Despite the years that have passed, the home remains one of the more talked-about properties in Palm Springs.Years after Bob Hope lived there, the house continues to draw attention. Its unusual shape, desert setting and famous ‘UFO House’ nickname have helped make it one of Palm Springs’ most memorable celebrity homes.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Director of new ‘Narnia’ movie takes heat over casting of Meryl Streep as Christ-like lion Aslan
articles.summary: Petition launched to replace "Narnia" director Greta Gerwig over casting of Meryl Streep as Christ-like lion Aslan.
articles.body: Criticism over the recent casting of actress Meryl Streep as the voice of the Christ-like lion Aslan in Netflix’s "Narnia" adaptation has continued as some Christian and media figures question the choice. An online petition is also calling on Netflix to replace director Greta Gerwig for future "Narnia" films. The petition, entitled, "Demand Netflix to replace director of the Narnia films," was started Friday on Change.org following negative reactions from some Christian fans and critics to the theological implications of a actress voicing Aslan, an allegory for Jesus Christ. "Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew," written and directed by Gerwig ("Barbie"), is based on the 1955 novel, the sixth published and first chronologically in the children’s book series "The Chronicles of Narnia" by British author, literary scholar and Christian thinker C.S. Lewis. FANTASY DOESN’T NEED ANOTHER 'GAME OF THRONES.' IT NEEDS WHAT TOLKIEN UNDERSTOOD The film is set to hit theaters Feb. 12, 2027, and Netflix on April 2, 2027, but it was the recently announced casting of Streep that brought renewed attention to concerns from some Christians about altering the voice of Aslan, a character Lewis presented as a Christ figure in Narnia. Movieguide founder Dr. Ted Baehr, who served as president of the Episcopal Radio-TV Foundation after it helped produce CBS’s classic 1979 animated adaptation of "The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe," said he was confused by the choice. DIRECTOR OF NEW ‘LORD OF THE RINGS’ REJECTS ‘POLITICALLY CORRECT’ CASTING AFTER SUGGESTIONS FILM IS TOO WHITE "When I did it, they had a hundred million or more people who had read ‘Chronicles of Narnia.’ Now I'm sure it's double or triple. And most of them know that Aslan is a Christ figure, and we understand that Christ in the Revelation gets married to the church, that he's a guy, but he's fully God and Holy man. We understand all that, so with the change that they're doing, it's going to alienate a lot of Christians," Baehr told Fox News Digital. Baehr, who noted that he spoke briefly with Gerwig about the film and that the 43-year-old filmmaker told him that, as a young woman, his version was her favorite, said she "comes at it from a different point of view." COMEDIAN LEANNE MORGAN CALLS OUT HOLLYWOOD FOR LIVING IN A 'BUBBLE' AND MISJUDGING WHAT AUDIENCES WANT TO SEE "That doesn't mean that it won't do well at the box office, it just means that there will be an extra audience, maybe 110 to 140 million Christians that may not show up because they don't like that," Baehr said. "But you know, you can build a movie with a lot of one group or another, so it doesn't mean the movie won't succeed, it just means it'll lose an audience." In his case, Baehr said he fought to ensure Aslan remained an uncompromised allegory for Jesus Christ in the 1979 adaptation. KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS IT'S 'EXHAUSTING' WHEN MOVIES TRY TO ALTER HISTORY TO FIT MODERN TASTES For her part, Gerwig, who has described herself as a Unitarian Universalist and churchgoer, has said she envisions her version as a "rock opera" and explained to entertainment site Empire that she wanted someone who was "profound but not pretentious, who had gravitas but not morose self-seriousness" to play the part of Aslan — someone, she said, "who could communicate depth and pathos as well as joy and delight." She added, "I wanted someone who was older than 70, so there was a wisdom of experience, but who also had the capacity of fresh wonder, like a child. And also to be one of the greatest actors to ever do it. That list is not a long one." CHRISTOPHER NOLAN CALLS CRITICISM OF 'THE ODYSSEY' CASTING DECISIONS 'IRRELEVANT' Fox News Digital reached out to Gerwig’s agent, Creative Artists Agency CEO and co-chairman Bryan Lourd, for further comment. Fox News Digital also reached out to Netflix for comment. Ned Lott, a casting and voice director and producer who has worked in the animation industry since 2000 with companies ranging from Disney to Warner Bros. and Nickelodeon on projects including 2025’s animated "David" and 2005’s "The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe," recalled his experience casting Aslan for the 2005 film. EVERY CONTROVERSY SURROUNDING CHRISTOPHER NOLAN'S 'THE ODYSSEY' FROM CASTING TO COSTUMES "It’s like casting for the voice of Jesus, or the voice of God. Like, in my mind, it was very important that the character of the books, and the integrity of the books, matched the voice, and even the actor," he told Fox News Digital. Lott said that when it came to casting Aslan for the 2005 film, he and his team auditioned dozens of British actors. But with just 24 hours left to make a decision, no one was completely satisfied. CHRISTOPHER NOLAN FACES GROWING BACKLASH OVER 'ODYSSEY' CASTING, HISTORICAL ACCURACY AS SCREENINGS CANCELED "It still wasn't like a slam dunk, you know. And so, it was just this kind of moment where I was leaving work and I was like, I literally talked to God. I said, ‘Okay, we have to find your voice, and I have one more day. So I need some help, you know.’ And I got in my car, I turned on the radio and all of a sudden there was the voice," Lott recalled. "Like, literally, there was the voice of Aslan, and I didn't know who it was." He did know it was a movie trailer for the 2005 film "Kingdom of Heaven," and so, after arriving home, he looked up the film on IMDb and saw that it was Liam Neeson, an Irish actor who had never appeared on their list of British celebrity thespians. The rest is history, with Neeson famously voicing Aslan in three "Chronicles of Narnia" films. Lott explained that casting is about the character rather than the performer and that there are instances in which a man has successfully voiced a female character. He cited director Brad Bird’s portrayal of Edna Mode in "The Incredibles" as one example. Lott said such casting is typically done for comedic effect. Additionally, Lott cited tricks that can be done with pitch shifting and EQ settings, as well as a voice actor’s performance, that can leave audiences unaware that the voice actor is a different gender from the character. Still, he said, this casting of Streep as Aslan leaves him puzzled. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We took so much care with Aslan and really understood him. It just seemed like a choice that we would have not made back in 2005 because we understood the integrity of the books and tried to do as much as we could with the integrity of what the author had in mind," Lott said. "So, it’s just like a different philosophy. It’s not something I’m used to. Clearly, there’s an artistic reason."

articles.title: Michael Douglas confirms secret affair with Kathleen Turner on 'Romancing the Stone' set
articles.summary: Michael Douglas reveals in his memoir, "One Helluva Ride," that he and Kathleen Turner kept their "Romancing the Stone" affair secret for 40 years.
articles.body: Michael Douglas is confirming a rumor that has followed him around for decades. In an excerpt from his upcoming memoir, "One Helluva Ride," the 82-year-old actor revealed that he and Kathleen Turner had an affair while filming "Romancing the Stone," a rumor they denied for over 40 years. "Kathleen was smart, funny, and sexy with a deep, sultry voice that became her signature," he wrote in an excerpt obtained by People. "I instantly liked her, and we were immediately attracted to each other." He went on to say that although he was married to Diandra Luker at the time, "things at home were in a bad place" and both he and Luker "were both having extramarital affairs." MICHAEL DOUGLAS' ACADEMY AWARD-WINNING ROLE IN ‘WALL STREET’ WAS FIRST OFFERED TO THESE TWO A-LIST ACTORS Douglas wrote that he left home to film the 1984 movie "still technically married, but separated," and that while audiences were "certain for years that we were in a relationship together" while making the movie, they denied it, even through the making of the sequel and years later when they reunited on "The Kominsky Method." The two would tell the public that while they "had amazing chemistry" and were "both tempted," they never acted on their feelings. "The truth is that during the production of Romancing the Stone, Kathleen and I fell hard for each other and began a relationship," he wrote. "It wasn’t a fly-by night affair; it grew naturally from how closely we were working together, how much pressure we were under, how much we respected and cared for one another, and how attracted we were to each other. Like every other guy in the world at the time, I was knocked sideways by Kathleen." He noted that the two of them kept their affair a secret for 40 years in order to protect Luker and their son, Cameron. "There were no cameras in elevators, no assistants using cell phones to take pictures," he said. "As Jack and Joan were falling in love, Kathleen and I were keeping the chemistry alive." Turner and Douglas decided to end things after Luker visited them on set with Cameron, "and made it clear to her [Turner] that we were still married." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? I love Michael and I look forward to enjoying the book." articles.title: Malayalam viewers hail Ajay Devgn's 'Drishyam 3', say this Hindi version 100 times better than the Mohanlal starrer: 'They wrote it so brilliantly'
articles.summary: Ajay Devgn-starrer ‘Drishyam 3’ is witnessing a strong response at the box office ever since its release on Friday.
articles.body: Ajay Devgn-starrer ‘Drishyam 3’ is witnessing a strong response at the box office ever since its release on Friday. While the film has been receiving praise from Hindi-speaking audiences, its reception in Kerala has also caught attention. A section of Malayalam viewers has been particularly impressed by the film’s writing and conclusion, with some even comparing it favourably with the Malayalam version starring Mohanlal.A Malayalam content creator recently shared his reaction to ‘Drishyam 3’ in a video, admitting that audiences in Kerala have traditionally been dismissive of the Hindi adaptations of the franchise. However, he said the third instalment changed his perception, particularly because of the way the story was written and brought to an end.Praising the film, the content creator said in Malayalam, "Those Hindi guys gave such a good conclusion to Drishyam. Just think about it, I hadn’t watched the first and the second part of the Hindi version. We used to look down on it like - 'Whatever who has the time to watch Hindi films.' I had that contempt, but in the end, I had to clap after watching part three of Drishyam in Hindi. Unbelievable. Jeethu Joseph (director of original Malayalam version of Drishyam), doesn’t even have 1% of the writing credit for this movie, because they themselves wrote and set the whole thing up. They wrote it so brilliantly."He further explained that while the film follows a distinctly Hindi commercial-film template, its treatment of the central characters and thriller elements worked for him. He added, “It’s a pure Hindi film template, occasional jokes, and camera style that felt like a serial quality, but still there are high moments. There are thrill elements, things that the Drishyam characters intend to do are all present in this film, that is why I am saying I am happy. I’m not saying everyone will watch this and be mind blown, but this makes sense. It’s not some crazy, mind-bending twist and turn, but they ended it really well as a proper continuation of part two.”The video also sparked a debate among viewers in the comments section. One user compared the two versions and wrote, "I feel D3 Malayalam is like a soap opera... Hindi is 100 times better than this." Another commented, "Malayalam drishym 3 was utter flop." A third viewer said, "Malayalam drishyam 3 felt like it was made more for business than for audience satisfaction." One user even joked, "Why don’t we remake the Hindi third part back to Malayalam."However, not everyone agreed with the comparison. Several viewers continued to back Mohanlal's performance as Georgekutty. One comment read, "No one can match Laletten's Georgekutty Emotions. Just making a better twist doesn't mean film can be compared." Another viewer said, "No one can beat Mohanlal sir when it comes to performance."Unlike the first two Hindi instalments, which were direct remakes of Mohanlal's Malayalam ‘Drishyam’ films, ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ follows an original storyline and has a different ending. Director Abhishek Pathak has previously spoken about taking a separate route for the third film. Ajay Devgn has also revealed that he sought Mohanlal's approval before proceeding with the new story, with the team deciding not to directly remake the Malayalam third instalment.Meanwhile, ‘Drishyam 3’ opened to a strong response at the box office. According to Sacnilk, the film collected Rs 66.75 crore net in India on its opening day, while its worldwide gross was estimated at Rs 95.10 crore. articles.title: Sanjay Dutt says he doesn't feel peace in India anymore, talks about PM Narendra Modi as Munnabhai, has THIS message for Donald Trump: 'Mamu zyada tante nahi paalne ka'
articles.summary: Sanjay Dutt recently revisited one of his most iconic characters, Munna Bhai, for a satirical take on Indian politics.
articles.body: Sanjay Dutt recently revisited one of his most iconic characters, Munna Bhai, for a satirical take on Indian politics. During an appearance on Shekhar Suman’s show ‘Shekhar Tonite’, the actor was asked to imagine himself as the Prime Minister of India for five minutes. What followed was a humorous monologue delivered in the familiar language and mannerisms of Munna Bhai.The Gandhi Jayanti special episode, released on Friday, saw Sanjay blend humour with references to Mahatma Gandhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump. Through his imagined speech, the actor touched upon the prominent display of political leaders’ photographs in public spaces, foreign trips and Trump’s tariff policies, while making a case for Gandhi’s philosophy of “Gandhigiri” over confrontation.The segment came after Sanjay spoke about the current state of the country and expressed his wish for Indians to experience greater peace. He said, “The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I can’t feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shivji that those days come back soon.”When asked to imagine himself as the Prime Minister and address the nation, Sanjay immediately slipped into his Munna Bhai persona.“Chalo desh mein kuch to chal rehla hai. Mere pyaare deshwasiyo, aaj apun aapka PM banke khub khush hua. Bole to body mein ajeeb type ka tarang daud re la hai. Bole to itna bada desh hai, itne saare log hain aur ab hum sabki zimmedari apun ke upar (My dear countrymen, today I am very happy to have become your PM. There is a strange kind of energy running through my body. This is such a huge country, there are so many people, and now the responsibility of all of them is on me).”He then joked about staying in India rather than travelling abroad to celebrate becoming Prime Minister, making an indirect reference to PM Modi.“Lekin aap log ekdum tension nahi lene ka. Apun is khushi ko celebrate karne videsh nahi jaane wala hai. Apun idharich rahega, aap sab logon ke beech. Nahi to PM aur janta mein connection kaise banega (But you people don’t have to worry at all. I am not going abroad to celebrate this happiness. I will stay right here, among all of you. Otherwise, how will there be a connection between the PM and the people?)”Sanjay then invoked Mahatma Gandhi and the three monkeys associated with his teachings, while suggesting that people should not simply remain silent when they witness something wrong.“Apun Gandhi ji ko bahut maanta hai. Aur Gandhi ji ke teen bandar sabko pata hai — bura mat dekho, bura mat suno, bura mat kaho. Lekin aaj ek chautha bandar bhi mangta hai. Bura dekhega to use theek kaun karega? (I really believe in Gandhi ji. Everyone knows his three monkeys — don’t see evil, don’t hear evil, don’t speak evil. But today I want a fourth monkey too. If someone sees something wrong, who will correct it?)”“Teeno bandar aankh, kaan, munh band karke baith jayega to desh kaise chalega, saala? (If all three monkeys sit with their eyes, ears and mouths shut, then how will the country function?)”The actor also poked fun at the widespread presence of the Prime Minister’s photographs, saying that the country should take precedence over an individual’s image.“Aur apun ko desh ke liye bahut kuch karne ka mauka mila hai PM banke, to apun ek aur kaam karega. Jahaan jahaan uska photo laga hai na, apun usko ekdum kam kar dega. Desh ko desh ka photo dikhna chahiye. (I have got the opportunity to do a lot for the country as a PM, so I will do one more thing. Wherever PM’s photograph has been put up, I will reduce it. The country should see a picture of the country.)”He continued, “Jahaan apna photo lagane ka mann karega na, wahaan Gandhi ji ka photo lagane ka. Bole to Gandhi ji ke vichar dekhna zyada zaroori hai. Apun ka photo dekh ke janta kya karega? (Wherever I feel like putting my own photograph, I will put Gandhi ji’s photograph there. Gandhi ji’s thoughts are more important. What will the people do by looking at my photograph?)”“Bole to apna photo to apun baad mein bhi khichwa sakta hai na, lekin desh ko pehle frame mein lagane ka. (I can get my photograph taken later as well, but the country should be put in the frame first.)”Turning his attention to international affairs, Sanjay brought Donald Trump into his fictional PM speech, referring to the US President as “Trump mamu”.“Aur agar desh ko frame mein laana hai to thoda duniya ko bhi frame mein laana padega na. Bole to apun dekh raha hai ki Trump mamu puri duniya ko out of frame karne mein laga hai. (And if we want to bring the country into the frame, then we will have to bring the world into the frame too. I can see that Trump mamu is trying to push the whole world out of the frame).”He then used his signature humorous style to suggest dialogue and diplomacy instead of threats and conflict.“Dekho Trump mamu, zyada tante nahi paalne ka. Duniya mein missile waise hi bahut ho gaya hai. Ab thoda pyaar bhi export karne ka. Kahin missile bhejne ka mann kare to pehle guldasta bhejne ka. Kisi ko dhamki dene ka mann kare na to use phone karke ghar bulane ka aur chai peete-peete baat suljhane ka. (Don’t create so much trouble. There are already enough missiles in the world. Now export a little love too.If you feel like sending a missile somewhere, send a bouquet first. If you feel like threatening someone, call them home and resolve the matter over a cup of tea.)”He wrapped up the satirical segment with a reference to another popular Munna Bhai catchphrase, saying, “Apun aa rela hai America, tumko jaadu ki jhappi dene.(I am coming to America to give you a jaadu ki jhappi.)”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Splice CEO Kakul Srivastava thinks AI emails are killing conversations
articles.summary: As head of Splice, CEO Kakul Srivastava has tried to carefully thread the line on AI music tools. She also hates her cup warmer.
articles.body: Kakul Srivastava is the CEO of Splice, the sample platform countless producers rely on for one-shots and melodic loops. Samples pulled from the service have found their way into massive hits like Lisa’s “Money” and “Espresso” by Sabrina Carpenter. (The original samples are here and here, for the curious.) Before that, Kakul held executive roles at Flickr, Yahoo, GitHub, and Adobe. Throughout her career, Kakul has found herself at the intersection of Silicon Valley and creatives. That’s been especially true at Splice, where she’s not just expanded the platform’s footprint by acquiring Spitfire Audio, but also overseen its forays into the world of generative AI. Last year, she was very outspoken on an episode of Decoder about avoiding the sort of “push-button, get-song” AI that has made companies like Suno so controversial. And based on her answers to our questionnaire, it doesn’t seem like her skepticism has waned. When it comes to Splice, the company has made a point of trying to offer AI products that still keep the human at the center of the creative process. And when it comes to communicating with colleagues, Kakul sees the same need to keep AI at bay. What is your most indispensable tool? A well-written document and a real conversation about it. Splice is remote-first, so we don’t have a hallway. What we have instead is somebody sitting down and actually thinking something through, and then a bunch of people arguing with it. Almost everything good that’s happened here started that way. Which is why I’m careful about AI-written documents. Once you can’t tell whether there’s a person behind the words, the conversation you have about it becomes a different conversation, and a worse one. And you can’t really go back from that. I think the same thing is true of music. What is your happy place online? Instagram, which I know is not the fashionable answer. My feed has turned into almost entirely people making music in ways I would never have thought of. There’s gothic western, which I did not know was a thing. There’s a woman in Russia who organizes street dancing. There’s a guy playing modern hits on a hammered dulcimer. The Indian chai-wala rapping. I could watch it all, all day. What game do you have the fondest memories of? Antakshari. It’s an Indian game — you sing a bit of a song, and whatever letter the line ends on is the letter the next person has to start their song with. You play it on long car rides, at weddings, any time a group of people is stuck somewhere together. I love that the whole game is made out of music and none of the players are musicians. You just have to remember, and you have to be willing to sing in front of your family, which for most people is the harder part. And then when you watch people’s faces get soft when the song really hits — even when it’s sung badly. That’s the power of music. What’s the most disappointing gadget you’ve owned? A cup warmer. It warms the cup. It does not warm the coffee. I want to be clear that it works exactly as designed. What creation are you most proud of? I can’t not say my kids. Watching a person go from nothing to a fully formed human with opinions you did not give them is the most amazing thing I have been anywhere near. And the strange part is that it isn’t rare. It’s happening in every house on the street. We all just watch it happen and then go about our day. Which are you least proud of? I was on the early team at Tiny Speck, the company that later became Slack. Before Slack, we made a game called Glitch — a massively multiplayer open world — and it was one of the most beautiful things I’ve ever worked on. The art, the sound, the writing, the way the world actually worked. Some of the most talented people I’ve ever been around. It failed, and it failed for reasons that were sitting right there in front of us. It was built on Flash, and Adobe had already stopped investing in Flash. It was a PC experience at the exact moment the whole world was moving to playing games on a phone. Two enormous tectonic trends, and we didn’t account for either one in time to do anything about them. I feel like I let down the creativity of the people who built something beautiful. What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received? Say the thing, then explain it. Don’t lay all your proof out first, hoping it earns you the right to make your point. Nobody is listening to the proof yet. They’re listening for whether you sound like you believe it. The confidence you say it with is what makes room for the explanation. What is your current obsession? Cooking my mother’s food. She died before I learned most of it from her, so I’ve been reconstructing her recipes off YouTube — strangers in their own kitchens, making the thing the way their mothers made it. It takes a lot of tries. I got one of them right last year, and the taste put me straight back to being eight years old with my mom by my side. This is what I think about when people ask me what technology is for. Some guy uploaded a video of his family’s recipe and gave me my mother’s cooking back. He will never know that. What do you think is worth splurging on? Live jazz. There is nothing else like being in a room where people are making decisions in real time and can’t take them back. I travel a lot for work, and if there’s any way to get to a show in whatever city I’m in, I’ll do it, even when it means I’m useless the next morning. What would the tagline for your biopic be? articles.summary: From Teresa Giudice's daughter to NeNe Leakes' son and Kim Zolciak's son, multiple "Real Housewives" kids have faced serious criminal charges.
articles.body: Teresa Giudice recently claimed daughter Milania, 20, had "fentanyl in her system" during an incident at the Tampa International Airport. Months before, Milania was arrested on an assault charge in New Jersey stemming from an alleged dispute. Her brush with the law is only one of many instances where the children of "Real Housewives" stars made headlines without the help of reality television cameras. REALITY STAR CLAIMS DAUGHTER, 20, HAD 'FENTANYL IN HER SYSTEM' IN AIRPORT BODYCAM Teresa, 54, attempted to explain her daughter's behavior during an encounter with officers at a Florida airport last month, according to bodycam footage obtained by Page Six. Milania fired back in the footage, and said, "Cause I was laced ... I go to college," before her sister Gia told her, "You're reckless." REALITY STAR'S SON, 15, INDICTED ON 7 COUNTS STEMMING FROM ALLEGED ASSAULT It’s unclear when exactly the fentanyl incident occurred and what substance Milania was allegedly given or who she believed was responsible. At the beginning of the bodycam footage obtained by Page Six, Milania could be heard requesting to speak to her mother. One officer asked Milania to sit back down and reminded her that she was "not controlling the situation." The "RHONJ" star shared a lengthy statement on social media Monday after the bodycam footage was released. "As a mother, there is nothing more important to me than the health, safety, and well-being of my children," she wrote. "The past few months have been incredibly difficult for our family, and I feel it is important to say something while also protecting my daughter during an extremely vulnerable time in her life." The "RHONJ" star explained that Milania had "experienced tremendous heartbreak and significant psychological trauma after losing two of her best friends," but was making sure she was "surrounded by love, family, support, and the care she needs." Milania pleaded not guilty in June to a simple assault charge in New Jersey following her arrest the month before. According to Page Six, her next court hearing has been postponed until Dec. 1. 'PIONEER WOMAN' REE DRUMMOND'S SON ARRESTED ON DRUG, ASSAULT CHARGES KJ Biermann, 15, was indicted last month for child molestation and multiple charges of sexual battery against a child under 16, according to documents obtained by Fox News Digital. A grand jury in Fulton County, Ga., indicted KJ (whose full name is Kroy Jagger) on a total of seven counts, which also included aggravated sodomy and a false imprisonment charge. REALITY STAR SAYS 'RHOC' COST HER MARRIAGE AS DAUGHTER SHUNS SHOW AFTER MILITARY HUSBAND'S PORTRAYAL The son of "Real Housewives of Atlanta" star Kim Zolciak and Kroy Biermann was arrested in August and initially charged with two felony counts stemming from an alleged April incident, according to documents obtained by Fox News Digital. Zolciak previously denied the allegations levied against her son in a statement provided to Fox News Digital. KJ was granted a $200,000 bond in September. KJ is the oldest son of Kroy Biermann and Kim Zolciak. The former couple also has Kash, 14, and twins Kaia and Kane, 12. Biermann adopted Zolciak's daughters, Ariana and Brielle, from a previous relationship. The pair each filed for divorce in 2023 after 11 years of marriage. "RHOA" star NeNe Leakes' son, Bryson Bryant, was booked on a contempt of court charge in July, according to TMZ. articles.title: 'Anupam Kher's first marriage to actress Madhumalti Kapoor ended in a day,' recalls his brother Raju Kher: 'He was quite seedha for that time'
articles.summary: Anupam Kher’s first marriage to actress Madhumalti Kapoor lasted only a few days, according to his brother and actor Raju Kher.
articles.body: Anupam Kher’s first marriage to actress Madhumalti Kapoor lasted only a few days, according to his brother and actor Raju Kher. Raju has now recalled how the couple, who had been together for around two to three years, decided to get married at a temple in Lucknow, only for Anupam to leave shortly afterwards.Speaking to Siddharth Kannan, Raju revealed that Anupam walked away from the marriage almost immediately after the wedding. He said the actor spent a day or two in Lucknow before leaving, eventually returning to Shimla and later heading to Delhi.“It ended in one day. They got married at a temple in Lucknow. The next day, he left from there, saying, ‘I cannot stay here.’ Anupam had first come to Shimla for a few days and then went to Delhi,” Raju said.According to Raju, Madhumalti was the one who brought up the idea of marriage after the couple had been in a relationship for several years. Anupam agreed, and the two decided to get married almost immediately.“They had been in a relationship for two or three years. She reached there and said, ‘Let’s get married.’ He said, ‘Okay, let’s do it tomorrow,’ and they got married. They must have stayed there for a day or two, and then he left,” he recalled.The marriage took place before Anupam had begun his career in Hindi cinema. At the time, he was in Lucknow, while Raju was in Shimla. Anupam subsequently moved to Mumbai to pursue acting and made his screen debut in Mahesh Bhatt’s ‘Saaransh’ in 1984.Raju said the family was not even aware that Anupam had got married at the time, as none of them had been present at the ceremony. He was asked how they reacted when Anupam left the marriage so soon.“Nobody from the family was there, so we did not even realise that he had got married,” Raju said.He also made it clear that he chose not to question his brother about the reasons behind the separation, leaving it to Anupam and Madhumalti to deal with what had happened between them.“Anupam was quite seedha for that time, while Madhu ji was a somewhat strong woman. Only they know what happened between them. I did not want to probe into it either. I thought, this is his life and he has to live it. If he ever needs me, as his brother, I will always be there,” he said.Madhumalti later married writer-director Ranjit Kapoor following her separation from Anupam. Raju also mentioned during the conversation that Madhumalti and Ranjit were together and had children.Madhumalti went on to remain active as an actor, working across Hindi films and television over the years.Anupam later found love again with actor Kirron Kher, whom he married in 1985. The two had known each other from their time at the Department of Indian Theatre in Chandigarh and were friends for several years before their relationship developed into a romance.Anupam has previously spoken about their relationship and recalled that marriage to Kirron was something he had never imagined, especially since she was one year senior to him at the theatre department.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Quote of the day by Meghan Markle: ‘It's our responsibility to make a choice on what we click on, we make a choice on what we read, we make a choice of what we engage in’ when the Duchess shares a message about positivity and personal choices
articles.summary: Meghan Markle emphasizes the importance of being selective about online content, encouraging individuals to focus on positivity and personal empowerment in a world overloaded with information.
articles.body: What we read, watch and respond to online can easily become part of our everyday routine. With so much information coming at us all the time, it can be difficult to decide what deserves our attention and what is better left alone. Meghan Markle once spoke about this very idea, encouraging people to be more careful about the content they allow into their lives.Today’s quote of the day by Meghan Markle reads: “It's our responsibility to make a choice on what we click on, we make a choice on what we read, we make a choice of what we engage in.”What does the quote by Meghan Markle mean?Meghan shared these words while speaking at an International Women’s Day panel at King’s College London on March 8, 2019. In her remarks, she went on to say that people can choose not to feed into negativity and instead be more positive and action-based. ITV reported her comments from the event, while King’s College London confirmed the International Women’s Day panel.Her message is fairly simple: we have some control over what gets our attention. That does not mean people can avoid every negative story or difficult conversation. Instead, Meghan was talking about making conscious choices. Before clicking on something, reading it or joining a conversation, people can stop and ask whether it is actually worth their time. A few minutes of scrolling can easily turn into hours of reading opinions, arguments and criticism. Meghan’s point was that people do not have to engage with everything that appears in front of them.Why does Meghan Markle’s message still matter today?The quote feels particularly relevant now because people spend so much of their day online. There is always something new popping up on our screens, whether it is a news story, someone’s opinion, a celebrity update or a comment. It’s easy to get pulled into it and keep checking what people are saying, even when we know we probably don’t need to. But doing that can also leave little room for the things that actually matter.Her message also connects positivity with action. For her, it wasn’t just about staying away from negativity. She also encouraged people to focus on things they care about and actually do something about them. That makes the quote less about ignoring problems and more about choosing where to put your energy. For students, creators and professionals, the thought can be useful in everyday life. Not every opinion needs an answer, and not every piece of online content deserves a reaction.Meghan Markle’s early lifeMeghan Markle was born on August 4, 1981, in Los Angeles, California. She developed an interest in acting and communication while growing up and studied theatre and international studies at Northwestern University.Before her royal life began, Meghan was already known to many viewers for playing Rachel Zane on 'Suits'. She also ran The Tig, a lifestyle blog where she wrote about travel, food, fashion and bits of her own life. It gave her a space to share her thoughts on subjects she cared about, including women’s rights and questions around identity.Meghan Markle’s rise to fameWho can forget the best paralegal from 'Suits'? Meghan as Rachel Zane in 'Suits' was able to establish herself as a household name. The show stayed on television for seven seasons. She was already known to fans of the series, but her relationship with Prince Harry later put her in the spotlight in a very different way. The couple married in 2018, and Meghan became the Duchess of Sussex. Her public work continued to include issues involving women, young people and community causes.Her 2019 International Women’s Day appearance came during this period, when she joined a panel discussing gender equality and women's empowerment. King’s College London says the event brought together speakers to discuss attitudes toward gender equality around the world. Looking back at Meghan’s words, the message is not really about staying away from the world. It is about being selective about what we allow to occupy our minds. In a time when there is always something new to read, watch or react to, choosing where to spend our attention can sometimes be just as important as choosing what we say.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 10-day Bengaluru Jaatre to bring citizens together
articles.summary: Karnataka govt announces Bengaluru Jaatre, a free 10-day citywide festival from Dec 4 with art, culture, food, heritage walks and community events across venues.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Seeking to foster a stronger sense of belonging among the millions who now call Bengaluru home, Karnataka govt announced Bengaluru Jaatre, a 10-day celebration of art, culture, food, heritage, music and community life, from Dec 4.Announcing the initiative Saturday, Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the city, which has grown into a global technology and economic hub, also needs spaces that bring people together and help residents connect beyond work and daily routines. “Bengaluru is much more than a place where we live and work. It is a city built by people from different languages, cultures and backgrounds. Bengaluru Jaatre is an opportunity for the city to come together and celebrate itself,” Gowda said.Unlike conventional festivals held at a single venue, the jaatre will be spread across the city with events planned at parks, lakes, playgrounds, educational institutions, museums, cultural centres and other public spaces. “There will be no single jaatre ground and no single central stage. Bengaluru itself will become the stage,” Gowda said.The festival is being modelled on Karnataka’s traditional oora habba or village fair, where entire communities come together to celebrate. The idea, officials said, is to recreate that spirit in a city of millions through the theme, “Many People. Multiple Cultures. One City.”Govt departments and agencies will organise a range of free-to-attend programmes, including music, dance, theatre, literature, heritage walks, exhibitions, food festivals and community events.
